entities.name: The Painter
entities.locs: The Painter is locked in the upper floor of the library at the end of the Corvian Settlement. Guarded by Sir Vilhelm, who must be defeated to obtain the key that unlocks the staircase to her location. After being freed from the library, she will move to the attic in Ariandel Chapel.
entities.plot:
The Ashen One first hears about the Painter while talking with Slave Knight Gael, the one she affectionately calls "uncle", at the Cathedral of the Deep. Gael mentions that "his Lady" resides in the cold land of Ariandel and claims that the Ashen One's role is to "show her flame". Similarly, the Forlorn Corvian Settler met in the Corvian Settlement shows his enthusiasm upon meeting the Ashen One, as this is the only person who can show "his Lady" flame.

The Painter was brought to the library's attic by Sir Vilhelm, who was guarding her and the key to her chamber. Vilhelm was acting on the orders of Sister Friede, who imprisoned the Painter with Father Ariandel's help. Ariandel is suppressing the Flame of the Painting with his own blood, hence only his and Friede's death can allow the Painter to see Flame. Upon being freed from house arrest, the Painter relocates from the library to the Ariandel Chapel attic. At the attic, she's found sitting in front of a big canvas; when spoken to, she divulges her vision of the new Painting. She emphasizes that the painting will show "a cold, dark, and very gentle place", which is going to be a good home for someone.

After the Ashen One finds The Ringed City, the Painter mentions that she is waiting to receive a pigment colored like the dark soul of man. It is the Blood of the Dark Soul, received after Gael's death by the Ashen One's hands. The pigment consists of dark souls consumed by Gael, with blood seeping from his body. After the Painter receives the pigment, she gently thanks the Ashen One and, now in possession of Flame and Dark, she finally starts work on her painting. She continues to await uncle Gael's return, unaware of his death.
entities.notes:
• The Painter is an infinitely respawning NPC.
  • Interacting with her isn't necessary to complete the DLC. She can even be ignored entirely in the library and still move to the attic once Sister Friede has been defeated.
  • Talking to her once she has moved to the attic, and then returning to the Corvian Settlement and talking to the Forlorn Corvian Settler rewards the player with a Titanite Slab.
  • Upon entering the Painted World of Ariandel, the Drowsy Forlorn, the first character met on a new path, refers to it as a "cold and gentle" and "fine" home for the forlorn, who have seen terrible things. However, he doesn't describe it as a "dark" place, despite being a "rotting bed" and just "fine" home compared to a "goodly" one, as planned by the Painter.
entities.desc: The Painter, also known as Ariandel's Lady is a character in Dark Souls III: Ashes of Ariandel.

entities.name: Unbreakable Patches
entities.plot:
As in previous Souls games, Patches attempts to fool or otherwise deceive the player into performing various actions which will allow Patches to attempt to kill them, in the aim of 'looting' their bodies afterward.

Cathedral of the Deep trap

Patches can be first encountered in the Cathedral of the Deep, after taking the elevator up near the entrance to the Deacons of the Deep boss room and opening the large double doors leading out to the rooftop mausoleum. He will be standing next to a bridge wearing the Catarina Set, attempting to trick the player into believing that he is a knight of Catarina and that he has spotted treasure on the other side of the bridge. Upon reaching the middle of the bridge, a cutscene occurs where Patches will lower it in an attempt to have the Giant Slaves kill the player. If they have already killed both giants, he will scold them for doing so.

At the end of the cutscene, Patches will remove the armor and relocate to the opposite side of the bridge, shortly before the room where Rosaria, Mother of Rebirth is met. The player can only access this area of the cathedral by taking the elevator up near the Cleansing Chapel and navigating the cathedral rooftops and catwalks before dropping down. Upon talking to Patches in this location, he will pretend as if he has never met the player before. Upon confronting him about the matter (e.g., choosing the "You know who I am" option), he will claim that the armor possessed him, and he will grant the player the "Prostration" gesture and a Rusted Coin as way of apology. After this, Patches will become a merchant.

The above encounter will not occur should the player take the elevator to the cathedral roof from the Cleansing Chapel and access that part of the cathedral first.

If Patches does not show up his first encounter will be at the Firelink Shrine trap.

Firelink Shrine trap

Patches can be encountered later at Firelink Shrine. If the player enters the tower adjacent to the shrine (the one which requires the Tower Key) and takes the elevator to the top of the belfry, Patches will close the gate and lock it behind the player. Returning to the gate and talking to Patches will cause him to taunt the player, stating his intention to loot the player's corpse when they die in the tower. The only way out is to reach the bottom of the tower by dropping down onto the coffins (Spook or Silvercat Ring will help) that stick out of the wall, or by using a bonfire warping ability (Homeward Bone, Darksign, Homeward, Coiled Sword Fragment). Alternatively, dying will simply respawn the player at the most recent bonfire, most likely that within Firelink Shrine.

Upon returning to the initial meeting place, the player can re-open the gate but Patches will be gone; he will have relocated to the upper level of the shrine, on the right side near the Giant Tree (the player may need to leave and re-enter the area, triggering a loading screen in the process, to cause him to spawn there). If the player confronts him here and refuses to forgive him, he will give them with a Rusted Gold Coin as a form of apology, and will provide his mercantile services here for the remainder of the game. Should the player have not encountered him in the Cathedral of the Deep, he will also teach "Prostration" here.

Upon reloading the area, talking to Patches while he is squatting at his usual location will reward the player the "Patches squat" gesture.

Rescuing Greirat

Talking to Patches while he is a merchant at Firelink Shrine will reveal that he and Greirat of the Undead Settlement are acquaintances. If the player has sent Greirat to pillage Irithyll of the Boreal Valley, Patches can be asked to save him. If the player has not purchased the full Catarina Set from Patches, and tells Patches about Greirat's whereabouts when asked (this occurs once an instance of Firelink Shrine has been loaded where Greirat has disappeared from his normal location), Patches will also disappear from Firelink Shrine. Upon beating an area boss while both are missing from Firelink Shrine (e.g. the location must be reloaded and Patches be absent from his spot), both Patches and Greirat will return.

A similar event occurs if Greirat is sent to pillage Lothric Castle; the player can choose to tell Patches of this, and he will leave Firelink until an area boss is defeated. Upon his return, he will sell a Hidden Blessing.

entities.name: Velka, the Goddess of Sin
entities.locs: The statue of Velka can be found within the sewers of the Undead Settlement, to which the Ashen One can pray for her favors. The Grave Key is required to unlock the door that gives access to the statue, which lies within the same tunnel system that leads to Irina's cell.
entities.desc: Velka, the Goddess of Sin is a character in Dark Souls III.

entities.name: Yoel of Londor
entities.quest:
Yoel is first encountered near the beginning of the Undead Settlement, at the edge of a crumbled bridge. The only survivor among many other less fortunate pilgrims like him, he seems enlightened to be in the presence of the Ashen One and asks if he could be allowed in their service. Agreeing to his plea will make him move to Firelink Shrine. There, he can be found on the lowermost level, at the end of the right corridor past Greirat, where he will sell an assortment of Sorceries to the player. Refusing his service will result in Yoel remaining in this spot, waiting for the Ashen One to change their mind.

Selecting the "Talk" option while in his interaction menu will teach the player the "Beckon" gesture. As a former sorcerer, all of his wares are sorceries.

Yoel also offers to level up the Ashen One without the use of souls. By selecting the "Draw Out True Strength" option, he will do so, functioning much like the Fire Keeper. Leveling up this way will place a Dark Sigil in the player's inventory. From this point onward, every time the player dies, they will gain a Hollowing level based on the number of Dark Sigils they possess. At 2, 6, 12 and 15 Hollowing, Yoel will again present the player with the option to level up for free, granting them an additional Dark Sigil each time up to a maximum of 5.

"Drawing Out True Strength" five times is necessary to complete Yoel's questline, which, together with the subsequent Yuria of Londor questline, lead to The Usurpation of Fire ending. It must be done before reaching the Catacombs of Carthus, since if Yoel is still alive when the player reaches said location, he will die the very moment the Catacombs are entered (including in the Settlement if he has not been recruited). If Yoel dies without having "Drawn Out True Strength" five times, or if the player heals their Dark Sigils with the Fire Keeper after she receives the Fire Keeper Soul, the Londor questline will have failed.

Yoel's dead body will be on the same spot he was when the Ashen One last saw him; uncharacteristically, his dead body will always remain, unless the player killed him themselves. If his questline was completed, Yuria will be next to his body, selling his old wares and allowing for the questline to continue. It is of note that killing Yoel after obtaining all five Dark Sigils does not void the questline, although there are no benefits to doing so.
entities.locs: He is first encountered near the Foot of the High Wall bonfire in the Undead Settlement, on the other end of the bridge from the gate leading into the settlement proper. The area is filled with dead pilgrims, although Yoel, located to the right, is still alive and can be talked to. He will offer to enter into Ashen One's service, and if the player accepts will move to Firelink Shrine. He can be found in the basement, at the end of the corridor on the west wing.

entities.notes:
• Upon reaching the Catacombs of Carthus, Yoel will die and his services will no longer be available, ending his questline prematurely unless the player has gotten all five Dark Sigils from him.
    • Yoel dies exactly the moment the "Catacombs of Carthus" banner appears on the screen, so it is perfectly safe to fight the Abyss Watchers beforehand and use the bonfire that appears after the battle, as long as the player does not descend the staircase that opens in that room. If you don't level up with him at all before he dies, it will cause the failure of Yuria's questline and the Londor Pale Shade to invade at two different points of the game.
    • The nature of the Pilgrims of Londor, and what the death they seek means to them, are left unexplained, but it is worth noting that if the player makes Yuria hostile, she claims that "Yoel knows not of thy folly," speaking of him in the present tense even though he will always have died by the time she appears.
entities.desc: Yoel of Londor is a character and merchant in Dark Souls III. He is voiced by David Sterne.

entities.name: Yuria of Londor
entities.locs:
Found in Firelink Shrine, at the end of the corridor on the west wing of the basement, in the same area where Yoel of Londor is found.

In order for Yuria to appear, the player must draw out their true strength (level up) with Yoel and acquire all five Dark Sigils before reaching the Catacombs of Carthus. The next time the player visits Yoel's usual place in Firelink Shrine, they will find him already dead with Yuria standing close by.
entities.plot:
Base game

Upon introducing herself, Yuria reveals that Yoel was a close friend to her and thanks the Champion of Ash for allowing him to be redeemed through his actions while at their service. She then does the same, pledging allegiance to the player and accepting them as her Lord and of all the hollows in Londor, in the hope that one day the Ashen One brings back its glory to the world.

Upon talking to her, the player will learn the "Dignified Bow" gesture.

Once Orbeck of Vinheim has moved to Firelink Shrine, Yuria will alert the player that he has proclaimed himself to be "Lord of Hollows," asking the player to settle the matter lest he imperil the player's rule. If the player brings Orbeck's Ashes to Yuria, she will reward them with the Morion Blade.

Once the player reaches the Catacombs of Carthus, Yuria reveals that she is also guiding Anri of Astora along the path to Irithyll of the Boreal Valley, and plans to engage him/her (gender is always the opposite of the player's) in matrimony. To this end, the player must aid Anri and keep him/her alive up until Pontiff Sulyvahn has been defeated (care must be taken not to kill the Londor Pilgrim within the Church of Yorshka). If successful, Anri may be found in the old Darkmoon tomb, Dark Sun Gwyndolin's boss arena in Dark Souls, and can be "married" here, gaining 3 more Dark Sigils for a total of 8.

Once the player completes their wedding vows, Yuria will swear her fealty to the true Lord of Hollows. She will no longer become aggressive if attacked by the player, short of the Dark Sigils being healed by the Fire Keeper. She will also make herself available to be summoned for the Soul of Cinder fight. Should she be summoned and survive this fight, her set and weapon can be found at her usual spot at Firelink Shrine.

If Yoel dies before the player can attain all five Dark Sigils, Yuria will not appear and the Londor Pale Shade will invade in the Farron Keep and Irithyll of the Boreal Valley; the Pale Shade will also invade the player at these locations should Yuria be killed or angered. Defeating the Pale Shade once will reward the Manikin Claws, while defeating them at both locations will cause the Pale Shade Set to appear at Firelink Shrine in the same area where Yuria and Yoel used to reside.

Conversely, if the player has not turned Yuria hostile, the Londor Pale Shade will become available for summoning in the aforementioned areas.

Yuria will disappear if Anri dies at any point before Pontiff Sulyvahn.

Completing Yuria's questline by Linking the First Flame while possessing 8 Dark Sigils unlocks the Usurpation of Fire ending.

Ashes of Ariandel

Yuria possesses additional dialogue should the player progress through the Painted World of Ariandel. After talking to Sister Friede and returning to Firelink Shrine, Yuria will recognize the scent of her sister, and warn the Ashen One of heeding their kindness over their principles.

Once Sister Friede has been defeated and the player is in possession of her soul, Yuria will remark on Elfriede's history with Londor, and request that the Ashen One usurp the First Flame in her memory.

Should the player have not yet acquired 8 Dark Sigils in either case, the dialogue will vary slightly.
entities.notes:
• Yuria will leave Firelink Shrine if the player talks to her after healing their accumulated Dark Sigil. If the player does not engage in dialogue with her after healing their Dark Sigils, Yuria will remain in Firelink Shrine indefinitely, though this serves no practical purpose.
  • Yuria only drops her ashes if the player kills her. As such, defeating the Soul of Cinder will mean that her wares are no longer available, unless she is killed before she has a chance to leave.
entities.desc: Yuria of Londor is a character and merchant in Dark Souls III. She is a mentor of the Sable Church and accomplished swordswoman, said to have claimed a hundred lives with her sword, the Darkdrift.

entities.name: Aldrich Faithful
entities.join:
To join the Aldrich Faithful covenant, the player must first have cleared the area by defeating both Sulyvahn's Beasts and then proceed to Archdeacon McDonnell's remains and pray to them, at this point they may ask to join and obtain proof of the covenant.

Killing the Sulyvahn's beasts is not required to join the covenant. If one wears the Slumbering Dragoncrest Ring and casts Hidden Body just as they reach the bottom of the ladder, they can sneak around the left, far wall and avoid the beasts and pray to McDonnell, thus joining.
entities.benefits:
Like the Watchdogs of Farron, Aldrich Faithful will be called upon to defend Aldrich's territory from trespassers; any player who has Host of Embers status will be subject to invasion. This area is defined as anywhere from the courtyard upon exiting Pontiff Sulyvahn's arena, up until the rotating stairway leading up to Anor Londo. Aldrich Faithful can pursue trespassers up into the cathedral itself, but will not be summoned for trespassers who have already reached the upper level bonfire.

Defeating the Host of Embers will reward all present Aldrich Faithful with Human Dregs, which can be offered to Archdeacon McDonnell to deepen their allegiance to the covenant.
entities.desc: Aldrich Faithful is a covenant in Dark Souls III.

entities.name: Blade of the Darkmoon
entities.page: Blade of the Darkmoon (Dark Souls III)
entities.join:
Obtained from Company Captain Yorshka upon talking to her and performing the "Darkmoon Loyalty" gesture at the Prison Tower in Irithyll of the Boreal Valley.

The tower can be reached via the rotating staircase that connects Irithyll to Anor Londo. An invisible pathway leading to the tower can be accessed from the lower level of the staircase when it is raised.
entities.benefits:
Blade of the Darkmoon functions identically to Blue Sentinels, where equipping the covenant item will place the player in a queue to be summoned into the world of a player who is affiliated with the Way of Blue should they be invaded by a red or purple dark spirit. In order to achieve victory, the player must defend the Way of Blue Adherent from the invading dark spirit, either by defeating the dark spirit or safely escorting the host into the boss fog of the area. Upon completion of their mission, the blue spirit will be rewarded with a Proof of a Concord Kept. If an Aldrich Faithful is slain, the blue spirit will be rewarded with a Proof of a Concord Well Kept.

Blue spirits will remain in the host's world so long as offending dark spirits are present, making it possible to obtain multiple Proofs in a single session. Blue spirits will not be summoned when Watchdogs of Farron or Aldrich Faithful invade a player's world through their covenant item.

Proofs may be offered to Yorshka to deepen allegiance to the covenant.

entities.desc: The Blade of the Darkmoon is a covenant in Dark Souls III.

entities.name: Blue Sentinels
entities.join: The covenant item is received by talking to Horace the Hushed at the Halfway Fortress bonfire in the Road of Sacrifices, or at Firelink Shrine after defeating the Deacons of the Deep. He will also drop the item if he is killed.
entities.benefits:
The Blue Sentinels are a covenant (along with the Blade of the Darkmoon) that puts special emphasis on aiding players in the Way of Blue covenant that have been invaded.

With the covenant item equipped, the player will be automatically summoned to the world of a Way of Blue Adherent who has been invaded by a red or purple dark spirit. After being summoned, the player, now a blue spirit, must protect the host and defeat the invader to receive a Proof of a Concord Kept before returning to their world. Alternatively, they can successfully escort the host to the boss of the area.
entities.rewards:
Once the player reaches Anor Londo, they may talk to Company Captain Yorshka and become a Blade of the Darkmoon, provided that they have obtained the Darkmoon Loyalty gesture. Proofs may be turned in to Yorshka in exchange for rewards.

entities.name: Mound-makers
entities.join:
The Mound-makers can be joined in the Undead Settlement. By navigating to a hidden area patrolled by numerous Thralls, the player can discover a non-hostile Hollow Manservant carrying an empty cage on its back. By examining the hollow, the player will enter the cage and be transported to the Pit of Hollows, below the Curse-rotted Greatwood's boss arena. This Manservant will be hostile if the Greatwood has been confronted or defeated, and thus cannot be interacted with.

Once there, the player must talk to Holy Knight Hodrick, who stands next to the covenant's Sacrificial Altar and who will give them the Mound-makers covenant item. If talked to again, he will give the player a Homeward Bone, which is required to leave the area without using the Darksign or committing suicide.

If the player has reached the second phase of the Curse-rotted Greatwood, killing Hodrick in the process, the only other way to join the covenant is to follow Sirris of the Sunless Realms' questline. Once Hodrick is defeated in Sirris's world, the covenant item will be rewarded.
entities.benefits:
When the covenant item is equipped, the player will take on the appearance of a Mad Phantom, and their summon sign and aura will take on a purple color. As a Mad Phantom, the player may invade or be summoned into a world, where they will be considered hostile by all other factions; if summoned via a White Sign Soapstone, basic enemies in the host's world will react to the player's presence.

In order to successfully complete an online session, the player must defeat either the Host of Embers, or a certain number of phantoms of any affiliation. Depending on the number of players already present in the host's world upon entering it, the requirement may increase to up to 3 phantoms. Therefore, unlike red invaders or blue territory defenders who must defeat the Host of Embers in order to achieve victory, a purple phantom may choose to slay phantoms allied with the host, or invaders who are attempting to defeat the host, and achieve their objective regardless. Conversely, however, the player must land the killing blow on a target to qualify, killing a target via secondary methods such as knocking them off of a cliff does not count.

Successfully completing an online session will reward the player with a Vertebra Shackle, which can be offered to the altar in the Pit of Hollows to rank up within the covenant. The method of entering the host's world has no effect on what the Mound-maker must do to complete the session.

Further rewards are granted upon leveling up:

entities.desc: The Mound-makers is a covenant in Dark Souls III.

entities.name: Rosaria's Fingers
entities.join: Talk to Saint Rosaria in the Cathedral of the Deep.
entities.benefits:
Single player

Talking to Rosaria allows the player to reassign their attribute points and change appearance a total of five times in one playthrough, at the cost of one Pale Tongue each.

After deepening allegiance with the covenant, players may summon Yellowfinger Heysel outside of the Keep Ruins bonfire, and be given the "Proper Bow" gesture. Deepening allegiance with the covenant is also required to progress Ringfinger Leonhard's questline.

Online play

Members of Rosaria's Fingers can invade or be summoned into the world of a Host of Embers via use of the Red Eye Orb or Red Sign Soapstone, respectively. In order to achieve victory, the player must defeat the Host of Embers. Doing so will reward all present covenant members with a Pale Tongue.

In the case of invasion, blue spirits from the Blue Sentinels and Blade of the Darkmoon may be summoned to aid the host if they are a Way of Blue Adherent. Should any of these blue spirits be defeated by any means (they are killed by enemies, the environment or a dark spirit), members of Rosaria's Fingers and any unaffiliated invaders will be rewarded with a Forked Pale Tongue.
entities.desc: Rosaria's Fingers is a covenant in Dark Souls III.

entities.name: Spears of the Church
entities.join: The player must simply equip the Spears of the Church covenant item.
entities.benefits:
While a Spear of the Church, the player can be automatically summoned to another player's world to be a boss in the Spear of the Church boss fight. While summoned as a boss, the player will be able to use the Ritual Spear Fragment and the Divine Spear Fragment.

Unlike other covenants, a Spear of the Church may be summoned in to combat a lone player who is not a Host of Embers, making this covenant the only one with such a mechanic in Dark Souls III.

The covenant is ranked up by offering Filianore's Spear Ornaments to the Divine Spear Monument outside the church where the Spear of the Church boss fight takes place.

entities.name: Warrior of Sunlight
entities.join:
The emblem to join the covenant can be found in the Undead Settlement, inside the leftmost house from the big open area with several peasants and an Evangelist praying at a burning tree.

Upon entering the house, head right and drop through a hole in the floor. The hole is partially concealed by several boxes and dead Cage Spiders. The covenant item is on a table along a wall opposite a fireplace with a cauldron of Estus Soup.
entities.benefits:
Joining the Warrior of Sunlight covenant will change the color of the player's summon sign from white to yellow, allowing hosts to easily distinguish them from other signs. Assisting a Host of Embers with the defeat of an area boss will reward the covenant member and the host with a Sunlight Medal as well as an Ember, and upon returning to their own world the player will automatically be granted their own Host of Embers status if they did not have it previously. Multiple Warriors of Sunlight in the same world will not increase the number of medals that are awarded.

Alternatively, players within this covenant can use a Red Eye Orb or Red Sign Soapstone to invade or be summoned into another player's world, as a red spirit that is distinguished by an orange glow. Defeating the Host of Embers will also reward the player with a Sunlight Medal.
entities.desc: The Warriors of Sunlight is a covenant in Dark Souls III.

entities.name: Watchdogs of Farron
entities.join: Found within the swamp of Farron Keep, the player must find a ladder surrounded by Rotten Slugs. Head up the ladder to find a large non-hostile wolf lying near a bonfire. Speak with the wolf to join the covenant and offer Wolf's Blood Swordgrass to rank up and receive rewards.
entities.benefits:
While the Watchdogs of Farron medallion is equipped, the player will be placed in a queue to defend the Crucifixion Woods area from trespassers. Once an Embered player steps foot in the swamp beyond the Halfway Fortress bonfire, a Watchdog will be summoned through the covenant sigil into the world of the trespasser. While in the trespasser's world, the player must defend the Farron Keep area by defeating the Host of Embers. After defeating the host, the player will return to his or her world with a Wolf's Blood Swordgrass.

Watchdogs may pursue their targets to any point within the Road of Sacrifices past the Halfway Fortress, and into Farron Keep itself, however they will only be summoned if a Host of Embers has trespassed the upper swamp area, a Watchdog will not be summoned if a player is within the lower poison swamp zone.

entities.name: Way of Blue
entities.join: Given by Emma, High Priestess of Lothric Castle at the end of the High Wall of Lothric, along with the Small Lothric Banner.
entities.benefits: While having the 'Way of Blue' sigil equipped, the player will be aided by a Blade of a Darkmoon phantom or a Blue Sentinel phantom if invaded by a red or purple dark spirit. These blue spirits will return home upon death of the host, personal death, use of the Black Separation Crystal (either personally or by host), defeat of the invader(s) or successful passage of Adherent to the boss of the area.
entities.rewards: There is no ranking system in the Way of Blue covenant meaning there are no rewards aside from receiving aid while invaded.
entities.desc: The Way of Blue is a covenant in Dark Souls III.

entities.name: Ancient Dragon Greatshield
entities.desc:
A wooden shield bearing the image of an ancient dragon. Very slowly regenerates HP.
The painting is the result of an exquisite but painstaking technique.
Lingering, undying traces of the ancient dragons can still be seen in their descendants, the man-serpents, though they have fallen far from grace.
Skill: Weapon Skill
Equipping this shield in the left hand allows one to perform the skill of the right-hand weapon.
entities.avail: Found in Archdragon Peak, behind the first Giant Man Serpent standing on top of a big archway, just before the entrance to the Ancient Wyvern's boss battle.

entities.name: Anri's Straight Sword
entities.desc:
Sword precious to Anri, another Unkindled. The dullest type of blade found in the ruined land of Astora.
Only, it was once the sword of an earnest noble figure, and its attacks are boosted by that elusive, essential property unique to humans: luck.
Skill: Stance
While in stance, use normal attack to break a foe's guard from below, and strong attack to slash upwards with a forward lunge.
entities.avail:
• Dropped by Anri of Astora upon killing them.
  • Found on Anri's corpse in Smouldering Lake if they are told of Horace's location without killing him.
  • Given to the player by Ludleth of Courland after assisting Anri in defeating Aldrich, Devourer of Gods in their world.
    • If following this method and Ludleth dies before the player obtains the sword, it will become unobtainable.
  • Found within Gwyn's honorary tomb in Irithyll of the Boreal Valley if Yuria of Londor's questline is being followed. After performing the marriage ritual on Anri's corpse, reload the area.
entities.notes:
• Regenerates a constant 2 HP per 2 seconds while equipped.
  • Inflicts 10% bonus damage against undead enemies.
  • It cannot be infused, but it is buffable by spells and items.

entities.name: Aquamarine Dagger
entities.desc:
A dagger fitted with aquamarine crystal.
Engraved with a prayer in the old tongue to ward off incident. Perhaps it was a parting gift given to one sent off on great travels.
Skill: Crystal Blade
Release magic for the aquamarine crystals, creating a fleeting blue crystal blade, lengthy enough to swing as a straight sword.
entities.avail: Found in The Dreg Heap. After the initial drop-down from the Stone-humped Hag's perch, there is a path right that leads further down, and a path left that leads to an elevated battlement guarded by a Harald Legion Knight. The item can be found in an area up the stairs behind the Harald Knight.

entities.name: Arbalest
entities.desc:
The largest crossbow, and suitably powerful for its size.
The bow string is made of metal, requiring great strength to fire.
Skill: Tackle
Lunge into a shoulder tackle, pushing back enemies to create distance.
entities.avail:
• Cathedral of the Deep
    • Dropped by crossbow-wielding Devouts of the Deep.
    • At the very top of the Cathedral that leads into the rafters, after taking an elevator up from the second shortcut, head down a path along the second flying buttress after crossing from the elevator tower. The Arbalest can be found at the end.

entities.name: Archdeacon's Great Staff
entities.desc:
Large staff bestowed upon Archdeacons of the Cathedral of the Deep.
The Archdeacon McDonnell's trespass, the sin of channeling faith for sorcery, transformed what was once merely a symbol of ecclesiastic authority into a catalyst for sorceries.
Skill: Steady Chant
Boost the strength of sorceries for a very short period. Works while equipped in either hand.
entities.avail: Obtained by reaching Rank 2 in the Aldrich Faithful covenant.

entities.name: Arstor's Spear
entities.desc:
One of the curses that festered within the belly of the Greatwood, and a terrible weapon favored by Earl Arstor the Impaler.
The spear is enwreathed in rotten, heavily poisonous meat. Defeating foes restores HP.
Skill: Shield Splitter
Take a large step forward and make a single focused thrust to puncture enemy shields and inflict damage.
entities.avail: Obtained by transposing the Soul of the Rotted Greatwood with Ludleth of Courland for 1,000 souls.

entities.name: Astora Greatsword
entities.desc:
This greatsword, bestowed only upon elite knights, is a relic of the ruined land of Astora.
Designed for a focus on thrust attacks, this sword is hard and sharp, but not unusually heavy.
Skill: Charge
Hold sword at waist and charge at foe. Use strong attack while charging to extend the length of the charge.
entities.avail:
Found in the Cathedral of the Deep.

From the Cleansing Chapel, head toward the graveyard and follow the first pathway on the left. The sword is on a corpse in front of a big tombstone, guarded by a kneeling Reanimated Corpse.
entities.notes: • Despite being said to be focused on thrust attacks, its moveset is relatively unchanged for its weapon class. Even stranger, its rolling attacks are overhead slams while many other ultra greatswords have thrusts.

entities.name: Astora Straight Sword
entities.desc:
A well-crafted sword named after the ruined land.
Astora, before its fall, was a land replete with royal blood, and this weapon is both a reminder and heirloom of that era.
Skill: Stance
While in stance, use normal attack to break a foe's guard from below, and strong attack to slash upwards with a forward lunge.
entities.avail: Found in the High Wall of Lothric, on a path hidden behind some barrels after passing through the rooftop area, inside a chest after one drops down to the scaffolding below.

entities.name: Avelyn
entities.desc:
An extremely rare rapid-firing crossbow.
Fires three successive bolts by means of an elaborate mechanism. Inflict heavy damage by making all three shots count.
Despite its use as a weapon, this crossbow is also a priceless work of art, and it bears resemblance to a musical instrument.
Skill: Tackle
Lunge into a shoulder tackle, pushing back enemies to create distance.
entities.avail:
Found in the Grand Archives, on top of a bookshelf on the right wing of the building.

Make way through the initial section of the archives and to the third floor, passing by the big wax container and a darkened room. Upon exiting the latter, head straight and either jump or roll diagonally and to the left from the top of the (kickable) ladder to land over a series of bookshelves where the crossbow lies.

It is advisable to equip the Silvercat Ring or cast Spook, and also deal with the Crystal Sage before attempting the jump.
entities.notes: • Can be traded with Pickle Pee in exchange for three Titanite Scales (only once per playthrough).

entities.name: Bandit's Knife
entities.desc:
A wide single-edged shortsword.
Primarily a slicing weapon, but its blade is crafted to cause bleeding, making it a favorite of lowly thieves and bandits.
Skill: Quickstep
Instantly step behind or around the side of foes. Especially effective when locked on to target.
entities.avail:
• Starting weapon of the Thief class.
  • Sold by Greirat of the Undead Settlement for 1,500 souls.
    • Sold by the Shrine Handmaid once she has been given Greirat's Ashes.
  • Dropped by Greirat only if the player did not buy any of these knives from him.

entities.name: Barbed Straight Sword
entities.desc:
Sword of Longfinger Kirk, the infamous Knight of Thorns. This sword's blade is lined with countless deadly thorns.
The thorns of this ominous weapon induce heavy bleeding.
Skill: Stance
While in stance, use normal attack to break a foe's guard from below, and strong attack to slash upwards with a forward lunge.
entities.avail: Found in the Cathedral of the Deep. Guaranteed drop from Longfinger Kirk, who invades as a dark spirit upon reaching the main open area located between the two Giant Slaves.

entities.name: Bastard Sword
entities.desc:
A widely-used heavy greatsword normally wielded with two hands.
Broad horizontal sweeping attacks make this sword effective against multiple enemies, but unwieldy in narrow spaces.
Skill: Stomp
Use one's weight to lunge forward with a low stance and increased poise, and follow with a strong attack for an upward slash.
entities.avail:
• Sold by Greirat of the Undead Settlement for 3,000 souls.
  • Sold by the Shrine Handmaid once she has been given Greirat's Ashes.

entities.name: Battle Axe
entities.desc:
Easily-wielded axe crafted for battle and inflicting standard damage. It's weight can be used to inflict high damage, but must be used carefully as it leaves its wielder open to retaliation.
Skill: Warcry
Let out a spirited warcry that temporarily boosts attack, and enables a special consecutive strong attack.
entities.avail:
• Starting weapon of the Warrior class.
  • High Wall of Lothric - A Deep Battle Axe is dropped by a Mimic found in a room below the fire breathing wyvern. The player can reach this place unharmed if they time their movements right between the wyvern's fire spewing.
entities.notes:
• The Deep Battle Axe found in the High Wall of Lothric has no scaling bonuses due to its infusion. However, it will still deal more damage to non-hollow enemies than most other weapons found early in the game.
    • The infusion can be removed by using a Shriving Stone with Blacksmith Andre, revealing the weapon's base stats and bonuses.

entities.name: Black Blade
entities.desc:
A short katana wielded by the swordsman and distinguished guest of High Lord Wolnir. This shiny black blade is thick, but shorter than the typical katana.
The swordsman was a master of a rare technique, traces of which can be observed in this weapon's strong attack.
Skill: Hold
Assume a holding stance to rapidly execute a lunging slash with normal attack, or a deflecting parry with strong attack.
entities.avail: Found in the Catacombs of Carthus, dropped by the Mimic at the end of the upper ledge surrounding the Demon, near the entrance to the Smouldering Lake.

entities.name: Black Bow of Pharis
entities.page: Black Bow of Pharis (Dark Souls III)
entities.desc:
A black longbow named after a hero of old. Known for the unusual stance from which it is fired.
Has a longer range than standard bows, but successful usage requires a trained, dexterous hand.
Skill: Pharis Triple-shot
Swiftly nocks three arrows with finesse after drawing the bow, firing them simultaneously.
entities.avail: Found in Farron Keep. On the far left side of the swamp, three Elder Ghrus can be found congregating near the flame closest to the Keep Ruins bonfire. One of them will automatically drop the bow into the player's inventory when killed.

entities.name: Black Iron Greatshield
entities.desc:
Greatshield made of black iron, deeply feared for its association with Knightslayer Tsorig.
Black iron offers high defense, and is particularly effective at warding off fire.
Skill: Shield Bash
Without lowering your guard, strike the enemy with the shield to knock them back or stagger them. Works while equipped in either hand.
entities.avail: Obtained by defeating Knight Slayer Tsorig by the large lava pool in the Demon Ruins, beneath the Smouldering Lake.

entities.name: Black Knight Glaive
entities.desc:
Glaive of the black knights who wander the lands. Used to face chaos demons.
The unique attack of this glaive greatly reduces enemy poise, reflecting the tremendous size of the enemies that the knights have fearlessly faced.
Skill: Spin Sweep
Sweep foes in a large spinning motion, and utilize momentum to transition into and overhanded strong attack slash.
entities.avail:
Located in the Untended Graves, in the same arena where Champion Gundyr is fought.

The halberd can be picked up before starting the boss fight. As one enters the arena, immediately turn right and hug the wall to find it.

entities.name: Black Knight Greataxe
entities.desc:
Greataxe of the black knights who wander the lands. Used to face chaos demons.
The unique attack of this axe greatly reduces enemy poise, reflecting the tremendous size of the enemies that the knights have fearlessly faced.
Skill: Warcry
Let out a spirited warcry that temporarily boosts attack, and enables a special consecutive attack.
entities.avail: Dropped from the Black Knights who wield the weapon in Smouldering Lake and Untended Graves.

entities.name: Black Knight Greatsword
entities.desc:
Ultra greatsword wielded by the Black Knights who wander the lands.
Designed to face chaos demons.
The Black Knights constantly faced foes larger than themselves, and this sword's unique attack greatly reduces enemy poise.
Skill: Stomp
Use one's weight to lunge forward with a low stance and increased poise, and follow with a crushing strong attack.
entities.avail: Dropped by the Black Knights who wield it. One can be found in the Road of Sacrifices, another in Smouldering Lake and two more in the Untended Graves.

entities.name: Black Knight Shield
entities.desc:
Shield of the Black Knights who roam the lands. A flowing canal is chiseled deeply into its face.
Long ago, the black knights faced the chaos demons, and were charred black, but their shields became highly resistant to fire.
Skill: Weapon Skill
Equipping this shield in the left hand allows one to perform the Skill of the right hand weapon.
entities.avail: Dropped by Black Knights.

entities.name: Black Knight Sword
entities.desc:
Greatsword wielded by the Black Knights who wander the lands. Designed to face chaos demons.
The unique attack of this sword greatly reduces enemy poise, reflecting the tremendous size of the enemies that the knights have fearlessly faced.
Skill: Perseverance
Raise sword in the name of the First Lord to temporarily boost poise. Damage reduced while activated.
entities.avail:
Found in the Smouldering Lake, behind an illusory wall.

From the Demon Ruins bonfire, descend two sets of stairs to reach a big room with two Demon Clerics. Turn right and proceed straightforward into a passage at the end. Hit the carved wall at the very end of this passage to reveal a hidden room with a Black Knight slaying a Ghru. The sword can be found inside.

entities.name: Blacksmith Hammer
entities.desc:
Metal hammer passed down amongst blacksmiths of the shrine. Serves as a strike weapon, but also excels at reducing poise and breaking the guard of a shield.
Of course, a hammer's true potential is realized in the hands of a blacksmith.
Skill: Perseverance
Assume an unfaltering stance of prayer to temporarily boost poise. Damage reduced while activated.
entities.avail: Found in the Untended Graves, lying on Andre's anvil at the spot where he normally can be found in Firelink Shrine.
entities.notes: • Can be traded with Pickle Pee in exchange for a Titanite Scale.

entities.name: Bloodlust
entities.desc:
Katana of the old Mound-Maker.
The Mound-Maker piled sacrifices upon the altar, but became the final offering himself, leaving this katana as a gift for his dear family.
Skill: Bloodlust
Stain blade with one's own blood to temporarily grant uncanny sharpness. For one driven by bloodlust, nothing deserves to remain standing.
entities.avail: Awarded for attaining Rank 1 in the Mound-makers covenant.

entities.name: Blue Wooden Shield
entities.desc:
A wooden shield painted bright blue, the symbol of clerics who have become undead. Close to a small shield in size.
Wooden shields are light, manageable, and offer relatively high magic absorption.
Skill: Parry
Repel an attack at the right time to follow up with a critical hit. Works while equipped in either hand.
entities.avail:
• Starting equipment of the Cleric class.
  • Found on a corpse in the graveyard in the Undead Settlement.

entities.name: Bonewheel Shield
entities.desc:
A giant wooden wheel, encircled by spikes and half-melded to a strange skeleton.
Can serve as a makeshift greatshield, albeit one with great gaps. Its true value is revealed through use of its Skill.
Skill: Wheel of Fate
Thrust out the wheel and give it a good spin, shredding enemies with the outer lining of spikes.
entities.avail: Dropped by Skeleton Wheels in the Catacombs of Carthus and the Smouldering Lake.

entities.name: Brigand Axe
entities.desc:
Axe favored by brigands of a distant land.
Surprisingly sturdy battle axe that requires more strength to wield than a standard axe.
Skill: Warcry
Let out a spirited warcry that temporarily boosts attack.
entities.avail: Found in the Road of Sacrifices, on a corpse behind the the madwoman, between the Road of Sacrifices and Halfway Fortress bonfires.

entities.name: Brigand Twindaggers
entities.desc:
These paired daggers are the preferred weapons of the brigands of a distant land.
When two-handed, the wielder holds a blade in each hand, allowing for divergent attacks that include left handed moves.
Skill: Quickstep
Instantly step behind or around the side of foes. Especially effective when locked on to target.
entities.avail: Found in the Road of Sacrifices, on a corpse behind where the madwoman spawns.

entities.name: Broadsword
entities.desc:
A straight sword with a broad blade designed for slashing.
A large sweeping attack makes this effective against crowds, but is prone to deflection from walls in narrow spaces.
Skill: Stance
While in stance, use normal attack to break a foe's guard from below, and strong attack to slash upwards with a forward lunge.
entities.avail: Found in the High Wall of Lothric, beyond the Tower on the Wall bonfire, in the room where Greirat's cell key is found. The corpse holding it is found in a small room in which a longsword-wielding hollow is found guarding it.

entities.name: Broken Straight Sword
entities.desc:
A straight sword with a broken blade.
A weapon with no exceptional qualities. Only a mad Hollow would choose to fight with this.
Skill: Stance
While in stance, use normal attack to break a foe's guard from below, and strong attack to slash upwards with a forward lunge. Only, neither move will appear very impressive with a broken sword.
entities.avail:
• Dropped by Hollow Soldiers and Praying Hollow Soldiers.
  • Cemetery of Ash
    • Found next to a gravestone after the Iudex Gundyr bonfire.
  • Road of Sacrifices
    • Dropped by Sage's Prentices.
  • Cathedral of the Deep
    • Dropped by Devout Bombers.
entities.notes:
• It shares the same weapon skill as the Long Sword, but with much lower reach and overall reduced effectiveness.
  • Despite the name, it appears to be a Long Sword with most of the blade broken off.
  • It has one of the lowest sell values in the entire game, beaten only by certain consumables like Cracked Red Eye Orbs.

entities.name: Buckler
entities.desc:
A very small round metal shield.
It features a large central protrusion designed for parrying attacks.
Skill: Parry
Repel an attack at the right time to follow up with a critical hit. Works while equipped in either hand.
entities.avail:
• Sold by Greirat of the Undead Settlement for 2,000 souls.
    • Sold by the Shrine Handmaid for the same price once she is given Greirat's Ashes.

entities.name: Butcher Knife
entities.desc:
Butcher's knife with an oddly large blade wielded by the madwoman haunting the Road of Sacrifices.
Squarely-landed hits restore HP.
Back in the Undead Settlement, the woman acquired a taste for human flesh, of which she took glee in partaking.
Skill: Sharpen
Sharpening the blade increases HP restored with each successful hit.
entities.avail: Dropped by Isabella the Mad in the Road of Sacrifices.

entities.name: Caduceus Round Shield
entities.desc:
Standard round wooden shield. It is decorated with twin snakes, an ancient symbol of the Great Swamp.
Wooden shields are light, manageable, and offer relatively high magic absorption.
Skill: Parry
Repel an attack at the right time to follow up with a critical hit. Works while equipped in either hand.
entities.avail:
• Starting equipment for the Pyromancer class.
  • Found in the Undead Settlement. At the junction with the Peasant Hollows and Evangelist praying before the burning tree, turn right and traverse through the stable areas. After defeating the Flamberge-wielding Thrall and opening the door, turn right and the shield can be found on a corpse.

entities.name: Caestus
entities.desc:
A fistfighter's weapon made from thick straps of leather studded with iron rivets.
When two handed, caesti are equipped in each hand.
Skill: Perseverance
Cross arms in front of the body to temporarily boost poise. Damage reduced while activated.
entities.avail: Found in the Undead Settlement, on a corpse in the sewers with several Hound Rats and one Giant Hound Rat, between Cliff Underside and Dilapidated Bridge bonfires.

entities.name: Caitha's Chime
entities.desc:
Sacred chime blessed by Caitha, goddess of tears. Rare even amongst Carim clerics.
Affected by intelligence, a rare thing for miracle catalysts, and also agreeable with miracles that lean towards the Dark. Its existence is concealed in the name of the Archbishop, as it is anathema.
Skill: Gentle Prayer
Recovers HP for a period of time, albeit extremely slowly. Works while equipped in either hand.
entities.avail: Found in Lothric Castle. In the small chapel prior to encountering the Dragonslayer Armour, there is an exit on the opposite side and a drop-down from a broken railing. Dropping down below, the chime can be found on a corpse lying above a group of Lothric Knights, in the area just past the moat guarded by the two Lothric Wyverns.
entities.notes: • Can be traded with Pickle Pee in exchange for the Help me! Carving (only once per playthrough).

entities.name: Canvas Talisman
entities.desc:
Medium for casting miracles of the Gods. Canvas talismans are austere items carried by heralds.
Equip a talisman or a sacred chime to cast miracles. Miracles must be attuned at a bonfire before use.
Skill: Unfaltering Prayer
Temporarily increase poise while casting miracles, preventing enemy attacks from interrupting prayer. Works while equipped in either hand.
entities.avail: • Sold by the Shrine Handmaid for 3,000 souls once she has been given the Paladin's Ashes.

entities.name: Carthus Curved Greatsword
entities.desc:
Large curved sword wielded by swordsmen of Carthus.
The lightest of the curved greatswords. Crafted to cause bleeding.
Skill: Spin Slash
Slice into foes with a large spinning motion, and continue spinning to transition into strong attack.
entities.avail: Dropped by the Skeleton Swordsmen who wield them in the Catacombs of Carthus.

entities.name: Carthus Curved Sword
entities.desc:
Curved sword of Carthus swordsmen.
This weapon's thick, heavy blade is crafted to cause bleeding, and requires ample strength and dexterity to wield effectively, suggesting that the swordsmen of Carthus were amongst the mightiest.
Skill: Spin Slash
Slice into foes with a large spinning motion, and continue spinning to transition into strong attack.
entities.avail: Dropped by Skeleton Swordsmen in the Catacombs of Carthus.

entities.name: Carthus Shield
entities.desc:
The tattered remnants of a leather shield used by a Carthus swordsman.
The swordsmen of Carthus were particularly agile, and this common shield is surprisingly light for one of medium size.
Skill: Parry
Repel an attack at the right time to follow up with a critical hit. Works while equipped in either hand.
entities.avail: Dropped by Skeleton Swordsmen in the Catacombs of Carthus.

entities.name: Carthus Shotel
entities.desc:
Strangely curved sword crafted to cause bleeding, wielded by Carthus swordsmen.
Shaped to sneak around the defenses of shields, this sword requires ample dexterity to wield effectively.
Skill: Spin Slash
Slice into foes with a large spinning motion, and continue spinning to transition into strong attack.
entities.avail: Dropped by the Skeleton Swordsmen who wield them in the Catacombs of Carthus.

entities.name: Cathedral Knight Greatshield
entities.desc:
A heavy iron shield used by the knights of the Cathedral of the Deep. The blessings of the Cathedral have granted it high dark absorption.
The face of the shield is decorated with the emblem of an old king of Lothric: a bold image of a great bird gazing skywards.
Skill: Shield Bash
Without lowering your guard, strike the enemy with the shield to knock them back or stagger them. Works while equipped in either hand.
entities.avail:
Cathedral of the Deep

  • Dropped by crossbow- and mace-wielding Cathedral Knights.

Consumed King's Garden

  • Dropped by mace-wielding Consumed King's Knights.

entities.name: Cathedral Knight Greatsword
entities.desc:
Ultra greatsword wielded by the knights of the Cathedral of the Deep.
Highly destructive if intolerably heavy.
Its blade is flattened for use as a strike weapon, but the point at the end allows for thrusting.
Skill: Stomp
Use one's weight to lunge forward with a low stance and increased poise, and follow with a strong attack for a spinning slash.
entities.avail:
Cathedral of the Deep

  • Dropped by Cathedral Knights who wield them.

Consumed King's Garden

  • Dropped by Consumed King's Knights who wield them.

entities.name: Chaos Blade
entities.desc:
A cursed sword of unknown origin bearing uncanny streaks on its blade.
Attacks also damage its wielder.
The sword is not unlike a thing misshapen, granted life, but never welcome in this world. In other words, chaos itself.
Skill: Hold
Assume a holding stance to rapidly execute a lunging slash with normal attack, or a deflecting parry with strong attack.
entities.avail: Found in the Untended Graves, uphill the left path before entering the remains of Firelink Shrine, on the same spot where the Sword Master was encountered in the Cemetery of Ash.

entities.name: Claw
entities.desc:
Weapon favored by intelligencers of an eastern land. The lacerations it inflicts do not mend easily.
When two-handed, claws are equipped to each hand.
Skill: Leaping Slash
Perform a forward leaping slash at the opponent's head. When successful, functions as a head shot, inflicting heavy damage.
entities.avail: Found in the Consumed King's Garden, beneath the central platform where a Consumed King's Knight stands guard and several Rotten Slugs lurk about.

entities.name: Claymore
entities.desc:
An unusually large and heavy greatsword normally wielded with two hands.
This highly versatile weapon can be swung broadly or thrusted.
Skill: Stance
While in stance, use normal attacks to break a foe's guard from below, and strong attack to slash upwards with a forward lunge.
entities.avail:
• High Wall of Lothric
    • Found at the end of the upper path where the fire-breathing Lothric Wyvern is encountered.
  • Irithyll of the Boreal Valley
    • Dropped by the Irithyllian Slaves who wield them.

entities.name: Cleric's Candlestick
entities.desc:
Candle stick used as both sword and catalyst. Used for worship by the Deacons of the Deep.
The deacons, under the guidance of Archdeacon McDonnell, became both clergymen and sorcerers.
Skill: Guiding Light
A candle provides a temporary source of light which reveals additional guidance.
entities.avail: Obtained by transposing the Soul of the Deacons of the Deep with Ludleth of Courland.
entities.notes:
• Despite being reinforced by regular Titanite, it cannot be buffed or infused.
  • It is the only soul-transposed weapon to not be upgraded with Titanite Scale.

entities.name: Cleric's Sacred Chime
entities.desc:
Sacred chime for casting miracles of the Gods. Chimes such as these are often given to clerics who become Undead.
Equip a talisman or a sacred chime to cast miracles. Miracles must be attuned at a bonfire before use.
Skill: Gentle Prayer
Recovers HP for a period of time, albeit extremely slowly. Works while equipped in either hand.
entities.avail:
• Starting equipment of the Cleric class.
  • Drops from the Gravetender Hollows in the Cemetery of Ash and Untended Graves.
entities.notes: • Can be traded with Pickle Pee in exchange for the Help me! Carving (only once per playthrough), provided that it has not been upgraded.

entities.name: Club
entities.desc:
A simple wooden club. Characterized by savage leaping attacks.
This crude bladeless strike weapon is effective against most foes, and can break the guard of a shield.
Skill: Warcry
Let out a spirited warcry that temporarily boosts attack, and enabled a special consecutive strong attack.
entities.avail:
• Starting weapon of the Deprived class.
  • Found in the High Wall of Lothric, located on the upper path where the fire-breathing wyvern is encountered.
entities.notes: Although Raw infusions are optimal at low Strength, it is always worth infusing the Club with a Heavy Gem over leaving it uninfused, even at the base requirement of 10 Strength.

entities.name: Composite Bow
entities.desc:
Composite short bow emphasizing power. Its size allows for quick shots.
Though more powerful than standard bows, it also requires more strength of the user, and its range is short.
Skill: Rapid Fire
Swiftly nocks arrows with finesse after drawing the bow, allowing for consecutive shots.
entities.avail: Sold by the Shrine Handmaid for 3,500 souls once she has been given the Dreamchaser's Ashes.

entities.name: Corvian Greatknife
entities.desc:
Dagger of the unwanted, those guided by heretical storytellers.
A rather large dagger with a powerful attack, but this transparent attempt to intimidate foes reveals much about its owner's fears.
Skill: Blind Spot
Use against shielded foes to break through their guard by attacking from the side.
entities.avail: Dropped by Corvians in the Road of Sacrifices, Farron Keep, Painted World of Ariandel and Untended Graves.

entities.name: Court Sorcerer's Staff
entities.desc:
Catalyst used by the court sorcerers of the Profaned Capital. Very powerful when wielded by an exceptionally intelligent sorcerer.
The court sorcerers laid claim to the legacy of the renowned Big Hat Logan, going so far as to emulate him with copies of the staff he used.
Skill: Steady Chant
Boost the strength of sorceries for a very short period. Works while equipped in either hand.
entities.avail: Dropped by a Mimic in the Profaned Capital, inside the second floor of the building within the Toxic swamp. It is guarded by a Monstrosity of Sin.

entities.name: Crescent Axe
entities.desc:
A crescent-shaped halberd resembling a long-handled battle axe.
Traditionally wielded by Way of White clerics.
Skill: Warcry
Let out a spirited warcry that temporarily boosts attack, and enables a special consecutive strong attack.
entities.avail: Sold by the Shrine Handmaid for 4,000 souls once she has been given the Paladin's Ashes.
entities.notes: • Unlike its previous appearances in the series, the Crescent Axe in Dark Souls III is a halberd, instead of an axe or a greataxe, and does not have an innate Magic infusion.

entities.name: Crescent Moon Sword
entities.desc:
Ringfinger Leonhard's weapon of choice, a type of shotel imbued with the power of the moon.
Leonhard set out on a journey of rebirth, but decided instead to serve the goddess as a knight, and inherited this weapon.
Skill: Crescent Blade
Assume a broad stance and fire off crescent moon blades.
entities.avail: Dropped by Ringfinger Leonhard, when defeated through using the Black Eye Orb in Gwynevere's chamber in Anor Londo.

entities.name: Crest Shield
entities.desc:
A knight's shield engraved with a crest.
One of the enchanted blue shields. The Crest Shield greatly reduces dark damage.
Skill: Parry
Repel an attack at the right time to follow up with a critical hit. Works while equipped in either hand.
entities.avail: Found in the Cathedral of the Deep. From the first bonfire, head towards the stairs but look for a path on the right. Follow it as it leads up the hillside, and the shield will be on a corpse at the top.

entities.name: Crimson Parma
entities.desc:
Standard round wooden shield. It is daubed with a red paint that symbolizes the blood of warriors.
Wooden shields are light, manageable, and offer relatively high magic absorption.
Skill: Parry
Repel an attack at the right time to follow up with a critical hit. Works while equipped in either hand.
entities.avail: • Sold by the Shrine Handmaid for 800 souls.

entities.name: Crow Quills
entities.desc:
Thrusting sword wielded by Corvian Knights, and a special paired weapon. When twin-handed, brandish four thin-edge blades in the left hand.
In their infatuation with Sister Friede, the Corvian Knights swore to protect the painting from fire, and to this end, took to the execution of their own brethren.
Skill: Quill Dart
Simultaneously throw temporarily substantial illusions of the four thin-edged blades wielded in the left hand.
entities.avail: From the Corvian Settlement bonfire, head out and across the bridge. Follow the wall of the house on your left until you see a smaller bridge. Go across and follow the path to the left. On your left you will see two entrances across a small gap. Jump it and go into the house on your right. Barrels will be blocking a platform that you need to run and leap off of and land on the elevated platform with the Crow Quills.

entities.name: Crow Talons
entities.desc:
Talons used by Corvian Knights. Inflicts five perpendicular slashes, causing heavy bleeding.
In their infatuation with Sister Friede, the Corvian Knights swore to protect the painting from fire and to this end, too to the execution of their own brethren.
Skill: Raptor Flurry
Spread right and left talons like a broad set of wings and launch into a tornado of consecutive attacks.
entities.avail: Found on the rooftops in the Corvian Settlement, guarded by two magic-wielding Corvians.
entities.notes: • The bleed build up of the Raptor Flurry is comparable to the bleed build up of the Frayed Blade's Hold skill.

entities.name: Crucifix of the Mad King
entities.desc:
A cross spear hung with a malformed corpse.
Once, a mad king was born to the pygmy royalty and Shira, knight of Filianore, put him to rest. But Shira's cross spear, unable to kill the undying king, only pinned itself to him. Shira delivered them together to the darkroom, where she stayed and held them close.
Skill: Mad King's Folly
Slam malformed corpse into the ground to briefly awaken it, then fillet with strong attack to trigger a roar, a blessing, or vexation.
entities.avail: Dropped by Shira, Knight of Filianore when she invades the player at Pygmy's Throne.

entities.name: Crystal Chime
entities.desc:
A sacred chime, once the possession of Gertrude, the Heavenly Daughter, and defiled by the scholars of the Grand Archives.
The power of crystals granted the scholars a degree of success. In this case, their work enabled this chime to be suitable for casting both miracles and sorceries.
Skill: Gentle Prayer
Recovers HP for a period of time, albeit extremely slowly. Works while equipped in either hand.
entities.avail:
Found in the Grand Archives.

From the first wax pool on the first floor, navigate to the right of the entrance to the dark room and look for a corridor, where a red-eyed spear-wielding Lothric Knight is making rounds. The chime is inside a small room at the end of the corridor.

entities.name: Crystal Sage's Rapier
entities.desc:
Thrusting sword with tiny crystals scattered across its blade, used by the Crystal Sages for self-defense.
The crystals boost the magic damage inflicted by the sword, and the item discovery of its wielder, fruits of the lifetime of research conducted by the sages.
Skill: Stance
From stance, use normal attack to back step and execute a surprise attack, or strong attack for consecutive thrusting.
entities.avail: Obtained by transposing the Soul of a Crystal Sage with Ludleth of Courland.

entities.name: Curse Ward Greatshield
entities.desc:
Greatshield given to those who resisted the curse long ago.
Far too heavy for an ordinary person, perhaps it signifies the foolishness of resisting the curse.
And yet, those who bear the weight of this shield will not find its protections against curses wanting.
Skill: Weapon Skill
Equipped this shield in the left hand allows one to perform the Skill of the right hand weapon.
entities.avail: Found in the Cathedral of the Deep, on a corpse lying in the mausoleum located in front of the pair of large doors at the end of the graveyard on the upper level, and above the shortcut ladder that leads down to the stream with the Corpse Grubs.

entities.name: Dagger
entities.desc:
Standard small dagger.
Small daggers lack power or reach, but can deal quick consecutive hits due to their light weight. Highly effective when used for critical hits, such as after parrying or attacking from behind.
Skill: Quickstep
Instantly step behind or around the side of foes. Especially effective when locked on to target.
entities.avail:
• Sold by the Shrine Handmaid for 300 souls.
  • Dropped by Hollow Assassins.

entities.name: Dancer's Enchanted Swords
entities.desc:
Paired enchanted swords that Pontiff Sulyvahn bestowed upon the Dancer of the Boreal Valley.
These blades, symbolic of the Dancer's vows, are enchanted with dark magic in the right-hand, and fire in the left, mirroring the Pontiff.
Skill: Dancer's Grace
Unleash the fury of both blades in a dancing spin motion and use strong attack to continue the performance until stamina is exhausted.
entities.avail: Obtained by transposing the Soul of the Dancer with Ludleth of Courland. No souls are required in the transposition process.
entities.notes:
• The magic sword is wielded in the main hand, and the fire sword is wielded in the off hand.
  • When equipped in the off-hand slot, the magic sword will be wielded, however when two-handed the swords will be equipped in their proper hands, with the off-hand holding the fire sword.
  • Use of the weapon's skill with the heavy attack exhausts not only stamina, but uses Focus Points, too, for the duration of the attack.

entities.name: Dark Hand
entities.desc:
Weapon that allows its wielder to evoke an art unique to Londor, the land of the Hollow. It is also said to be an ancient relic of a Primordial Serpent.
The Dark Hand mercilessly saps the essence of its victims, and can also double as a special shield. Cannot be used two-handed.
Skill: Lifedrain
Embrace the victim and steal their HP. Can only be used against humans.
entities.avail: Sold by Yuria of Londor for 12,000 souls.

entities.name: Dark Sword
entities.desc:
Pitch-black straight sword of the Darkwraith, survivor of the land swallowed by darkness.
The Darkwraiths were the first red orb invaders, and originators of a unique sword technique inspired by their thick, broad blades.
Skill: Stomp
Use one's weight to lunge forward with a low stance and increased poise, and follow with strong attack for an upward slash.
entities.avail: Dropped by Darkwraiths in Farron Keep and High Wall of Lothric.

entities.name: Darkdrift
entities.desc:
A cursed sword with an unseen blade, the choice weapon for Yuria of Londor.
Yuria, a mentor of the Sable Church and accomplished swordswoman, is said to have claimed a hundred lives with this weapon.
Skill: Darkdrift
Aim carefully, and pierce with a large forward lunge. The unseen blade penetrates straight through shields, for nothing can defend from Darkdrift.
entities.avail:
• Firelink Shrine
    • Dropped by Yuria of Londor.
    • Alternatively, left at her normal location once she disappears after completing the Lord of Hollows ending.

entities.name: Darkmoon Longbow
entities.desc:
Longbow of Darkmoon Gwyndolin. who was gradually devoured by Aldrich.
This golden bow is imbued with powerful magic and is most impressive with Moonlight Arrows.
Skill: Darkmoon Arrow
Infuse a readied arrow with Darkmoon essence, granting it magic damage and the ability to pierce shields.
entities.avail: Obtained by transposing the Soul of Aldrich with Ludleth of Courland for 5,000 souls.

entities.name: Demon's Fist
entities.desc:
A demonic fist that burns with fiery essence. Its wielder can release this power through use of its Skill.
When two-handed, fists are equipped in each hand.
Skill: Flame Whirlwind
Spin through opponents with abandon, flaming fists outstretched. Using a strong attack while spinning utilizes your momentum to slam the ground with both fists.
entities.avail: Obtained by transposing the Soul of a Demon with Ludleth of Courland.

entities.name: Demon's Greataxe
entities.desc:
This greataxe, a favorite among demons, contains the strength of fire.
The demons, born of Chaos, harbor fire, and yet they are twisted and malformed, such that they were never meant to be.
Skill: Demonic Flare
Briefly cause flame within to flare, and smash it upon earth and foes.
entities.avail: Transpose the Soul of a Demon with Ludleth of Courland.

entities.name: Demon's Scar
entities.desc:
This chaotic thing, the last flame kindled by the demon prince, is shaped like the claw marks of a demon.
It is both a fiery bladed weapon and pyromancy flame.
Skill: Spin Slash
Spin to stoke a fierce chaos flame, and use momentum to transition into a spinning strong attack, creating a short-lived lava pool.
entities.avail: Obtained by transposing the Soul of the Demon Prince with Ludleth of Courland for a cost of 10,000 souls.

entities.name: Dragon Crest Shield
entities.desc:
A knight's shield engraved with a crest depicting a dragon.
One of the enchanted blue shields. The Dragon Crest Shield greatly reduces fire damage.
Skill: Parry
Repel an attack at the right time to follow up with a critical hit. Works while equipped in either hand.
entities.avail: Found in Farron Keep. On the bridge above the Old Wolf of Farron bonfire, turn right and head towards the closed gate, then drop off the destroyed railing to the right. Navigate the platforms to reach the other side, the shield will be found on a corpse near the dead wyvern, amongst scattered Crystal Lizards.

entities.name: Dragon Tooth
entities.desc:
Created from an everlasting dragon tooth that will never break.
Left by Havel himself, along with his boulder-like great shield. Grants its wielder resistance to magic and fire.
Skill: Perseverance
Anchor weapon in earth to temporarily boost poise. Damage reduced while activated.
entities.avail:
• Only one per playthrough can be obtained at Archdragon Peak:
    • Dropped by Havel the Rock at the top of the Great Belfry.
    • The two Man Serpent Summoners have a small chance of summoning Havel as well.

entities.name: Dragonhead Greatshield
entities.desc:
This shield, as hard as a great boulder, is formed by the head of the descendant of an Archdragon.
The Ringed Knights, by command of the gods, stood amongst the ranks who set out to slay the dragons, but their contributions were never lauded.
Skill: Dragon Roar
Even the descendant of an Archdragon perishes not, and use of this skill restores its former strength, sending surrounding foes flying with a dragon roar.
entities.avail: Found in The Ringed City. Located beneath the bridge where Darkeater Midir is first encountered near the Ringed City Streets bonfire. The shield is guarded by a Ringed Knight.

entities.name: Dragonhead Shield
entities.desc:
This shield, as hard as a great boulder, is formed by the head of the descendant of an Archdragon.
The Ringed Knights, by command of the gods, stood amongst the ranks who set out to slay the dragons, but their contributions were never lauded.
Skill: Dragon Breath
Even the descendant of an Archdragon perishes not, and use of this skill restores its former strength, sweeping foes with a frontal exhalation of dragon breath.
entities.avail: Found in The Ringed City. Past the "Show your humanity" puzzle near the Ringed City Streets bonfire, proceed past the Judicator Giant and two Ringed Knights. After climbing down the ladder towards the Purging Monument, make a hard right before the bridge to the monument, and follow the path to a dead end where the shield can be found.
entities.notes: • Even if players run out of FP, they can still use the shield's skill; however, it will come at a damage penalty of about 50%.

entities.name: Dragonrider Bow
entities.desc:
Longbow of the Dragonriders, who served the Old King of Want.
The Dragonriders were the Old King's royal guard, and great strength was demanded of them. Merely drawing this bow calls for inhuman strength. The worthy few who can master this bow, however, use it to devastating effect.
Skill: Puncture
Pull the arrow even further back for a more powerful shot that can also pierce shields.
entities.avail:
Found in the Smouldering Lake.

From the Demon Ruins bonfire, make way to the lowest floor. Climb up the stairs after the area with several Basilisks and cross a bridge with a Black Knight standing guard at the other end. Climb up the two sets of ladders nearby, turn around and drop to a small niche on the right wall with a corpse holding the bow.

entities.name: Dragonslayer Greataxe
entities.desc:
Melted iron greataxe that once formed part of the Dragonslayer Armour.
Thickly imbued with the power of lightning. Use skill to draw upon the techniques used to slay the archdragons.
Skill: Falling Bolt
Hold axe high in air to gather fierce lightning, and smash ground to whip the bolts to the ground.
entities.avail: Obtained by transposing the Soul of Dragonslayer Armour with Ludleth of Courland.

entities.name: Dragonslayer Greatbow
entities.desc:
Greatbow used by the Dragonslayers during the age of gods. Far greater in size than any normal bow, and far more devastating.
The bow must be anchored to the ground when fired, a time-consuming operation that leaves the user vulnerable. Only specialized great arrows can be fired from the bow.
Skill: Puncturing Arrow
Masterfully fires off a great arrow that pierces through all enemies in its path, inflicting damage.
entities.avail:
Found in Irithyll of the Boreal Valley.

  • Dropped by Silver Knight archers.
  • One is found along with five Dragonslayer Greatarrows on a corpse lying beneath the flying buttresses where most of the Silver Knights are posted.

entities.name: Dragonslayer Greatshield
entities.desc:
Melted iron shield that once formed part of the Dragonslayer Armour.
The shield offers high protection to lightning, which the Dragonslayer commanded as his own, and its Skill has faint echoes of the Dragonslayer's own fighting style.
Skill: Shield Bash
Without lowering your guard, strike the enemy with the shield to knock them back or stagger them. Works while equipped in either hand.
entities.avail: Obtained by transposing the Soul of Dragonslayer Armour with Ludleth of Courland at Firelink Shrine.

entities.name: Dragonslayer Spear
entities.desc:
Cross spear associated with Ornstein the Dragonslayer. A weapon of the gods imbued with the strength of lightning.
Two-handed thrust utilizes the support of the cross and requires great might, but can pierce deep into the flesh of dragons, and send mere men flying.
Skill: Lightning Charge
Charge with spear at waist to enwreathe with lightning, then release bolts with final thrust.
entities.avail: Found in Archdragon Peak. From the Dragon-Kin Mausoleum bonfire, proceed up the nearby stairs and the spear can be obtained by interacting with the metal gate that leads to the courtyard below the Nameless King's arena.

entities.name: Dragonslayer Swordspear
entities.desc:
A dragon hunting weapon from the age of the gods. The earliest form of the cross spear, serving as both sword and spear.
Its owner was the Nameless King and deific hunter of dragons. The swordspear is imbued with lightning, of which he was the heir.
Skill: Falling Bolt
Hold swordspear high in the air to summon fierce lightning that descends upon distant foes.
entities.avail: Obtained by transposing the Soul of the Nameless King with Ludleth of Courland for 10,000 souls.

entities.name: Dragonslayer's Axe
entities.desc:
Axe favored by Creighton the Wanderer, infamous deserter of the Knights of Mirrah.
Called Dragonslayer's Axe for the lightning that pulsates within its blade, but Creighton used it to slay men.
Skill: Warcry
Let out a spirited warcry that temporarily boosts attack.
entities.avail: Obtained after defeating Creighton the Wanderer in Irithyll of the Boreal Valley. He will invade near a large tombstone outside of the Church of Yorshka and will only invade after defeating him with Sirris of the Sunless Realms on the bridge to Irithyll.

entities.name: Drakeblood Greatsword
entities.desc:
Greatsword wielded by an order of knights who venerate dragon blood.
This sword, its blade engraved with script symbolizing dragon blood, inflicts magic and lightning damage.
Skill: Stance
While in stance, use normal attack to break a foe's guard from below, and strong attack to slash upwards with a forward lunge.
entities.avail: Found in Archdragon Peak. Guaranteed drop from the first Drakeblood Knight spawned by the Man Serpent Summoner in the Dragon-Kin Mausoleum.

entities.name: Drang Hammers
entities.desc:
Paired hammers of the Drang Knights, proclaimed descendants from the land known for the legend of the Linking of the Fire. When the Drang Knights disbanded, they scattered across the lands as sellswords. They quickly became known for shieldless, aggressive tactics that struck fear into the hearts of men.
Skill: Spin Bash
Bash foes with a large spinning motion, and utilize momentum to transition into an overhanded strong attack smash.
entities.avail: Found in the Cathedral of the Deep by the staircase that leads to the Deacons of the Deep boss area, at the feet of a Giant Slave in a pool containing many Writhing Rotten Flesh and one Man-grub.
entities.notes: This weapon does very large amounts of Poise damage, useful against high poise enemies and bosses.

entities.name: Drang Twinspears
entities.desc:
Paired spears of the Drang Knights, proclaimed descendants from the land known for the legend of the Linking of the Fire. When the Drang Knights disbanded, they scattered across the lands as sellswords. They quickly became known for shieldless, aggressive tactics that struck fear into the hearts of men.
Skill: Charge
Hold spear at waist and charge at foe. Use strong attack while charging to extend the length of the charge.
entities.avail: Dropped by the Drang Knight who wields them in Irithyll of the Boreal Valley, in the courtyard after Pontiff Sulyvahn.

entities.name: Earth Seeker
entities.desc:
This large twin-bladed axe forged with bronze is a ceremonial weapon normally used in sacred rites.
Millwood is a land of primitive earth worship where chieftain knights served as high priests.
Skill: Earthen Wrath
Thrust weapon into earth with a prayer to trigger explosive tremors.
entities.avail: In the Snowy Mountain Pass area, inside the large valley area being patrolled by Millwood Knights and the large tree in the center. The Earth Seeker is within a cave area at the back of the valley, being guarded by a Millwood Knight who is himself wielding an Earth Seeker.

entities.name: East-West Shield
entities.desc:
A wooden shield decorated with the ancient symbol of the two-headed eagle. Close to a small shield in size.
Wooden shields are light, manageable, and offer relatively high magic absorption.
Skill: Parry
Repel an attack at the right time to follow up with a critical hit. Works while equipped in either hand.
entities.avail: Found in the Cemetery of Ash. Take the path on the left before entering Firelink Shrine; the shield can be looted from a corpse lying on the branches of a tree found before encountering the Sword Master.

entities.name: Eastern Iron Shield
entities.desc:
A thick, round metal shield decorated with the unique crest of an eastern land.
