entities.avail:
A minimum of eight are guaranteed to the player per playthrough.

  • Cemetery of Ash
    • At the far end of the side area guarded by the Ravenous Crystal Lizard.
  • Undead Settlement
    • To the side of the wide-open area where the Evangelist preaches before the burning tree. To the left are a large number of explosive barrels which hide a corpse that holds the item.
    • Above the Cliff Underside area, where Cornyx of the Great Swamp is encountered. In the wide-open area where Peasant Hollows throw Firebombs and a Hollow Manservant holding a pot guards the path, there is a corpse pinned under a torture rack that is holding the consumable.
    • On the path to the Dilapidated Bridge, there is an Evangelist that will cast Gnaw from very long range down a narrow road. To the right of the road at the start are some destructible barrels and crates that lead to a secret side path to avoid this barrage. Before a drop-down to the lower section of the road is a corpse holding the item.
    • On a corpse within the underground catacombs area that is accessed with the Grave Key. The corpse is located deep within the catacombs and is guarded by numerous skeletons.
  • Road of Sacrifices
    • Shortly after the Road of Sacrifices bonfire, it can be looted from a corpse next to the overturned carriage at the beginning of the path leading towards the Halfway Fortress area.
    • In the Crucifixion Woods area, after leaving the Halfway Fortress bonfire there is a series of small drop-downs to the right that can be traversed instead of the sloping path guarded by Lycanthrope Hunters. On the second drop-down there is a corpse that holds the item.
    • Past the Crucifixion Woods bonfire, instead of entering the ruins that lead to the Crystal Sage take the path to the right. There is a corpse in the open that can be looted for the soul, however it is also guarded by a Lycanthrope.
  • Catacombs of Carthus
    • Dropped by Giant Hound Rats.
  • Smouldering Lake
    • Dropped by Hound Rats.
    • Dropped by Giant Hound Rats.
  • Irithyll Dungeon
    • Dropped by Hound Rats.
    • Dropped by Giant Hound Rats.
  • The Ringed City
    • Dropped by White-faced Locusts.
entities.use: Consume to acquire 800 souls.

entities.name: Stalk Dung Pie
entities.usage: Turns enemy toxic, but also affects user
entities.desc:
Dried fecal waste material, marked by a long plant stalk that was not properly digested.
Throw behind at enemies to inflict toxin build-up, but also ups your own toxicity.
Strictly speaking, this consists of different material than the dung pie, but waste is waste, no sense in splitting hairs.
entities.avail:
• Firelink Shrine
    • Sold by the Shrine Handmaid for 50 souls each, once she has been given the Excrement-covered Ashes.
  • Irithyll of the Boreal Valley
    • Dropped by Giant Slaves.
entities.use: Drop behind the wielder to inflict 65 Toxic buildup but 0 damage to enemies behind the wielder, while also increasing Toxic buildup on self by 55.

entities.name: Throwing Knife
entities.usage: Throw at enemies to inflict damage.
entities.desc:
Small throwing knife.
Throw at enemies to inflict damage.
Most items choose their wielder, and only experience can improve their effectiveness.
True strength can be gained in no other way.
entities.avail:
• Firelink Shrine
    • Sold by Greirat of the Undead Settlement for 20 souls.
    • Sold by the Shrine Handmaid once she has been given Greirat's Ashes.
  • Can be farmed from Hollow Assassins or Devout of the Deep enemies.

entities.name: Undead Hunter Charm
entities.usage: Blocks Estus recovery within a limited area.
entities.desc:
Tool used to hunt down the Undead.
Blocks Estus recovery within a limited area.
Used long ago by Lloyd's cleric knights on their Undead hunts. Although Allfather Lloyd is long forgotten by the Way of White, his hunts have lived on, and this charm allows one to challenge Undead without fear of tenacious healing.
entities.avail:
High Wall of Lothric

  • Two can be found in a side room after climbing down from the rooftops and before the second Lothric Knight, who wields a spear.

Firelink Shrine

  • Sold by the Shrine Handmaid for 500 souls once she has been given the Paladin's Ashes.

Cathedral of the Deep

  • Dropped by Man-grubs.
entities.use:
Upon use, an Undead Hunter Charm is thrown to the ground, releasing a white cloud that affects anyone that is hit by it. Affected targets will have a debuff applied to them that prevents them from using their Estus Flask for 25 seconds. Healing Miracles may still be cast, however.

They may also be thrown at Mimics, forcing them to go into a sleeping state after which they can be looted safely. This effect can be used on Mimics in any state, whether they are waiting for prey or are actively attacking the player, and can be re-applied any number of times, dependent on the number of Undead Hunter Charms being carried.

When thrown at glowing-eyed Skeletons in Catacombs of Carthus, it will prevent them from reanimating, allowing them to be killed the first time around.

entities.name: Vertebra Shackle
entities.usage: Used to rank up in the Mound-makers covenant.
entities.desc:
A special bone collected by members of the covenant of Mound-makers, discovered in the corpses of their victims.
Only one such bone is found in the vertebrae, and the Mound-makers believe it to be a shackle of the gods. In their minds, each victim is another connection, an addition to the family.
entities.avail:
Single player:

  • Defeat Holy Knight Hodrick when he invades near the Dilapidated Bridge bonfire.
  • Dropped by Skeleton Swordsmen (rare).

Online gameplay:

  • Fulfill duty while invading as a mad dark spirit. This can be done by defeating the Host of Embers, or by defeating enough phantoms of any affiliation.
  • Defeat an invading mad dark spirit as any affiliation.
entities.use: <ol><li>Used to rank up in the Mound-makers covenant.</li> <li>Once per game cycle, one can be traded with the Nestling in exchange for Lucatiel's Mask.</li></ol>

entities.name: Wolf's Blood Swordgrass
entities.usage: Used to rank up in the Watchdogs of Farron covenant.
entities.desc:
A leaf signifying a duty fulfilled by the Watchdogs of Farron, who stand beside the old wolf to ensure the serenity of those at rest. Depicts a swordgrass leaf stained with dried blood.
Long ago, the swordgrass leaf quietly identified members of the Undead Legion. In the rotted forest rest the spirits of warriors past, their acceptance of and gratitude toward their guardians is expressed eloquently by the humble leaf.
entities.avail:
• Dropped by all variants of Ghrus in Farron Keep.
  • Rewarded for successfully destroying a Host of Embers when summoned to defend Farron Keep as a Watchdog of Farron.
entities.use: Offered to the Old Wolf of Farron in Farron Keep to rank up in the Watchdogs of Farron covenant.

entities.name: Yellow Bug Pellet
entities.usage: Boosts Lightning damage absorption for 60 seconds.
entities.desc:
Medicinal pellet made from crushed insects. The yellow type temporarily boosts lightning damage absorption.
The grave wardens of Carthus used these to repel a great sand worm.
The worm tumbled into the catacombs, and proceeded to dominate its new home in the Smoldering Lake.
entities.avail:
• Sold by the Shrine Handmaid for 1,500 souls each once she is given the Grave Warden's Ashes.
  • Dropped by Skeletons and Skeleton Swordsmen in the Catacombs of Carthus and Smouldering Lake.
entities.use: Boosts Lightning damage absorption by 15% for 60 seconds, 10% in PvP.

entities.name: Young White Branch
entities.usage: Allows the player to transform into an object that suits their current environment and blend with it.
entities.desc:
A young white branch.
Use to transform into something that blends in to the surroundings.
Little Dusk's first sorcerer's staff eventually became a seedling, and then three white birch saplings. The young branch is said to still contain echoes of little Dusk's capriciousness.
entities.avail:
• ×1 can be chosen as a burial gift at the beginning of the game.
  • Firelink Shrine
    • Sold by the Shrine Handmaid for 1,000 souls each, once she has been given the Xanthous Ashes.
  • Undead Settlement
    • ×3 can be found around the white birch at the graveyard past the Dilapidated Bridge.
    • ×1 is presented to the player as a "token of friendship" by the giant archer. If the giant turns hostile once more, he will present another branch each time he is befriended.
  • Cathedral of the Deep
    • ×3 can be found near the white birch at the small graveyard located in front of the cathedral.
  • Farron Keep
    • ×2 can be found in the poison swamp, near another white birch located to the left of the Keep Ruins bonfire (if looking toward the main gate). The area is comprised of deep water and is guarded by a Great Crab.
  • Painted World of Ariandel
    • One is found in the Corvian Settlement, to the right of the building where Sir Vilhelm is fought. it is guarded by a lone Birch Woman.
  • The Ringed City
    • Three are found in the Ringed City Streets, at the base of a white birch at the far end of the swamp guarded by numerous Hobbled Clerics.
entities.use: Allows the player to transform into an object that suits their current environment and blend with it, much like the Chameleon sorcery.

entities.name: Aldrich Faithful
entities.usage: Equip to join the Aldrich Faithful covenant.
entities.desc:
The holy symbol of the Cathedral of the Deep, and crest of those who see beyond fire to the age of deep waters. Equip to pledge oneself to the Aldrich Faithful covenant.
The faithful ensure that Aldrich, Devourer of Gods, remains undisturbed, by taking the form of loyal spirits and hunting down those who would trespass the ruined cathedral.
Summoning takes place automatically while this is equipped.
entities.avail:
Found in Irithyll of the Boreal Valley. Obtained by interacting with Archdeacon McDonnell's remains in the Water Reserve and accepting to join the Aldrich Faithful covenant.

From the Pontiff Sulyvahn bonfire, proceed through the level and make way to the opposite side of the big courtyard with several dead Giant Slaves. Enter the building at the end and hit the wall on the left to reveal a hidden ladder. Climb down and defeat the two Sulyvahn's Beasts lurking at the bottom. Once done, head to the far-left corner of the room to find McDonnell's remains.
entities.use: Equip to pledge oneself to the Aldrich Faithful covenant. Summoning takes place automatically while this item is equipped.

entities.name: Binoculars
entities.usage: Zoom in on distant scenery.
entities.desc:
Binoculars made of brass.
Use to peer at distance scenery.
Their utility is singular, but applications many. The value of these specs depends greatly on the imagination of their owner.
entities.avail: Found in the High Wall of Lothric. From the initial bonfire, head towards the dragon corpse and onto the battlements above. It can be found on a corpse at the top.
entities.use: Use the binoculars to peer into the distance: to gaze upon aesthetic views or to plan a route of attack.

entities.name: Black Eye Orb
entities.usage: Use to invade Leonhard in Anor Londo.
entities.desc:
Arcane orb left on Rosaria's corpse.
Have faith her soul can be retrieved, by invading the world of her killer, and returning victorious.
The Black Eye is proof of vengeance, but often appears serene as it casts its gaze toward Irithyll.
entities.avail:
Found in the Cathedral of the Deep. The player must first join Rosaria's Fingers and offer at least one Pale Tongue to rank up in the covenant. The player must then talk to Ringfinger Leonhard, who will appear at the entrance of Rosaria's Bed Chamber.

Once the player reaches Anor Londo and defeats Aldrich, Devourer of Gods, the orb can be found on the now-dead body of Rosaria.
entities.use: Used to invade Leonhard in the room above the Aldrich, Devourer of Gods bonfire (Gwynevere's chamber in Dark Souls). Upon defeating him in his world, the player will obtain the Soul of Rosaria, the Crescent Moon Sword and his Silver Mask.

entities.name: Blade of the Darkmoon
entities.usage: Equip to join the Blade of the Darkmoon covenant.
entities.desc:
A silver pendant depicting the Darkmoon and a sword, the crest of the Darkmoon Knights, the original Blue Sentinels. Equip to pledge oneself to the Blade of the Darkmoon covenant.
When a member of the Way of Blue faces a dark spirit, the Blades of the Darkmoon, by an ancient accord, help to root out the invader.
Summoning takes place automatically when equipped.
entities.avail:
The pendant is received from Company Captain Yorshka upon joining the Blade of the Darkmoon covenant in Irithyll of the Boreal Valley.

From the Anor Londo bonfire, proceed to the spiraling staircase (it must remain in its topmost position), go downstairs and exit by the lowermost part. A prison tower will be visible in the distance and to the right.

Walk straight forward into the void, revealing the existence of an invisible bridge that leads to the tower. Captain Yorshka can be found here, and the player may join her covenant if they have the "Darkmoon Loyalty" gesture. By performing the gesture for Yorshka within her dialogue menu, the player may receive the covenant item as proof of joining the covenant.
entities.use: Equip to pledge oneself to the Blade of the Darkmoon covenant. Summoning takes place automatically while this item is equipped.

entities.name: Blue Sentinels
entities.usage: Equip to join the Blue Sentinels covenant.
entities.desc:
Faded sheepskin parchment depicting the Darkmoon and a sword. Equip to pledge oneself to the Blue Sentinels covenant.
When a member of the Way of Blue is threatened by a dark spirit, the Blue Sentinels, in compliance with an ancient accord, assume the form of blue spirits, and help to root out the invader.
Summoning takes place automatically while this is equipped.
entities.avail:
• Gift from Horace the Hushed by talking to him at the Halfway Fortress or Firelink Shrine.
  • Dropped by Horace if he is killed at any point.
entities.use: Equip to pledge oneself to the Blue Sentinels covenant. Summoning takes place automatically while this item is equipped.

entities.name: Dragon Head Stone
entities.usage: Gain the head of a dragon and emit dragon breath.
entities.desc:
Stone imbued with the power of the everlasting dragons, used in a secret rite by dragon worshippers.
Gain the head of a dragon and emit dragon breath, a transformation that is irreversible until death.
Those who choose the path of the dragon strive for perfect imitation, and the dragon head rite is the first step in this grand process.
entities.avail: Obtained upon defeating the Ancient Wyvern in Archdragon Peak.
entities.use:
Upon activation, the player gains the head of a dragon and is able to breathe fire. This transformation is irreversible until death.

The absorption values for the head piece are as follows:

  • 4% Magic
  • 9% Fire
  • -4% Lightning
  • 4% Dark
  • +15 to all status effect resistance

Physical absorption remains at 0%, and all flat defenses remain penalized for the empty armor slot.

entities.name: Dragon Torso Stone
entities.usage: Gain the torso of a dragon and a dragon's roar.
entities.desc:
Stone imbued with the power of the everlasting dragons, used in a secret rite by dragon worshippers.
Gain the torso of a dragon and a dragon's roar, a transformation that is irreversible until death.
From ancient times, the path of dragon worship was walked by warriors. It is said they envision Archdragon Peak in the depths of their meditation, and at times, they even hear the distant sound of the great bell at the peak.
entities.avail: Found in Irithyll Dungeon, on a draconic statue looking out beyond the cliffside and performing the "Path of the Dragon" gesture. This is the same spot where the player may use the gesture to gain access to Archdragon Peak.
entities.use:
Upon first activation, the player's body mutates into a human/dragon hybrid form, a transformation that takes several seconds of stillness and is irreversible until death. Activating the Stone afterwards causes the Ashen One to roar like a dragon, unleashing a Force-like shockwave, and buffing their AR by 10% (12.5% in PVP) for five seconds.

Additionally, the player's absorption values for the chest, arms and legs pieces become as follows:

  • 13% Magic
  • 26% Fire
  • -11% Lightning
  • 13% Dark
  • +45 to all status effect resistance

These are compounded with the absorption values of the associated head piece, which is also equipped by default. Physical absorption remains at 0%, and all flat defenses remain penalized for empty armor slots.

entities.name: Filianore's Spear Ornament
entities.usage: Used to rank up in the Spears of the Church covenant.
entities.desc:
The Spears of the Church watch over the Princess' slumber, and this serves as proof of their fulfillment of their duty. The embellished gold cloth is woven with a crest of young grass.
The Princess' knights proudly displayed these precious flavors, which were most often seen swaying from their identical ceremonial spears.
entities.avail:
• ×1 obtained after defeating the Spear of the Church.
  • Reward for successfully defeating a Host of Embers as the Spear of the Church. Additional Ornaments are rewarded depending on the number of phantoms they have summoned.
  • Dropped by Ringed Knights.
  • One is found next to the ladder just before Midir's boss room.
entities.use: Used to rank up in the Spears of the Church covenant, being offered to the Divine Spear Monument outside the Church where the Spear of the Church takes place.

entities.name: Forked Pale Tongue
entities.usage: Use to acquire two Pale Tongues.
entities.desc:
Proof that a red eye orb invader successfully fended off a blue spirit.
Those who hunt dark spirits take the names of gods in ancient accord with the Way of Blue, a deception exemplified by their forked tongues.
Use to acquire two Pale Tongues.
entities.avail: Acquired by defeating a Blue Sentinel or Darkmoon Blade while invading as a red spirit that is not a Warrior of Sunlight.
entities.use: Use to acquire two Pale Tongues.

entities.name: Human Dregs
entities.usage: Used to rank up within the Aldrich Faithful covenant.
entities.desc:
Proof of a duty fulfilled by the Aldrich Faithful who patiently await the Devourer of Gods' return.
Dregs are the heaviest things within the human body, and will sink to the lowest depths imaginable, where they become the shackles that bind this world.
entities.avail:
• Obtained as a reward upon successfully defeating a trespasser while in the Aldrich Faithful covenant.
  • Irithyll of the Boreal Valley
    • Dropped by Deacons.
    • One can be found near the Water Reserve.
  • Anor Londo
    • Dropped by Deacons.
  • The Dreg Heap (The Ringed City)
    • Dropped by longstaff-wielding Murkmen.
entities.use:
Offer Human Dregs to Archdeacon McDonnell in the corner of the Water Reserve to rank up within the Aldrich Faithful covenant:

  • Offering 10 dregs rewards the player with Rank 1 and the Great Deep Soul.
  • Offering 30 dregs rewards the player with Rank 2 and the Archdeacon's Great Staff.

<tabber>Official translation= Proof of a duty fulfilled by the Aldrich Faithful who patiently await the Devourer of Gods' return.

Dregs are the heaviest things within the human body, and will sink to the lowest depths imaginable, where they become the shackles that bind this world. |-|Original description (Japanese) = エルドリッチの神喰らいを待ち続ける 神喰らいの守り手たちが、その使命を果たした証 人の内にある最も重いもの。人の澱み

それはどんな深みにも沈み 故にいつか、世界の枷になるという |-|Literal translation = Proof that Guardians of the God Eater, who continue to wait for Eldritch the God Eater, have fulfilled their mission. The heaviest thing within humans. The stagnation of humanity.

It will sink to any depth, so it is said that it will become the shackles of the world. </tabber>

entities.name: Loretta's Bone
entities.usage: Give to Greirat to progress in his questline.
entities.desc:
Old, discolored human bone with several holes bored into it.
A woman's corpse in the Undead Settlement was found clutching this bone. Her name was Loretta.
entities.avail: Found in the Undead Settlement, on a corpse hanging on the balcony of the first house after the Undead Settlement bonfire. The player needs to cut the body's ropes to make it fall, preferably by using a long reach weapon. The body can be looted once they have made their way to ground level.
entities.use:
• Give to Greirat in Firelink Shrine to progress through his questline.
  • Can be traded with Pickle Pee in exchange for a Ring of Sacrifice (only once per playthrough).

entities.name: Mound-makers
entities.usage: Equip to join the Mound-makers covenant.
entities.desc:
A malformed vertebra found by the mad, with a queer symbol on its inside, proof of the shackles of the Gods. Equip to pledge oneself to the Mound-makers covenant.
The mound-makers wish only to add to their mounds, becoming mad spirits whether summoned as co-operators or invaders.
They are blithe to those around them, for in their minds, any kill might lead to another shackle.
entities.avail:
Found in the Undead Settlement. Given by Holy Knight Hodrick after talking to him in the Pit of Hollows.

From the Undead Settlement bonfire, proceed through the level and in the big open area with praying Peasant Hollows and an Evangelist, turn right toward the stables. Instead of entering, break the crates on the right to uncover a hidden path guarded by numerous Thralls. Proceed through the area and drop to the other side, where a non-hostile Hollow Manservant with an empty cage paces about. Interact with the cage to be transported to the Pit of Hollows, where Hodrick awaits besides the Mound-makers' Sacrificial Altar.

Should the player have defeated the Curse-rotted Greatwood, this item is dropped by Hodrick when he is defeated alongside Sirris of the Sunless Realms during her questline.
entities.use: Equip to pledge oneself to the Mound-makers covenant.

entities.name: Proof of a Concord Well Kept
entities.page: Proof of a Concord Well Kept
entities.usage: Use to acquire two Proof of a Concord Kept.
entities.desc:
Distinguished proof that one has hunted the enemies of the gods, as per the ancient accord with the Way of Blue.
The layered ear of a dark spirit is the mark of a particularly guilty offender, one who has flagrantly violated one god or another.
Use to acquire two Proof of a Concord Kept.
entities.avail: As a Blue Sentinel or Darkmoon Blade summoned into the world of a Way of Blue adherent, this item is obtained by defeating a red invader who has equipped the Aldrich Faithful (item) covenant item.
entities.use: Use to acquire two Proofs of a Concord Kept.

entities.name: Rosaria's Fingers
entities.usage: Equip to join the Rosaria's Fingers covenant.
entities.desc:
Sacred seal of Archdeacon Klimt, who served Rosaria, Mother of Rebirth. Equip to pledge oneself to the Rosaria's Fingers covenant.
Rosaria's Fingers collect tongues in her name. Some do it to be reborn; others do it to help comfort their voiceless goddess.
entities.avail:
Found in the Cathedral of the Deep.

Given by Saint Rosaria in Rosaria's Bed Chamber after talking to her and accepting to join the Rosaria's Fingers covenant.
entities.use: Equip to pledge oneself to the Rosaria's Fingers covenant.

entities.name: Spears of the Church
entities.usage: Equip to join the Spears of the Church covenant.
entities.desc:
A green-rusted ornament of young grass, the crest of Princess Filianore. Equip to join the Spears of the Church's covenant.
The Spears of the Church watch over the Princess' slumber, and when the church is compromised by a trespasser, the Judicator summons them as loyal spirits to eliminate the threat. (Summoned automatically while this is equipped)
Loyal spirits summoned as Spears of the Church are granted a blessing of protection.
entities.avail: Obtained after defeating Darkeater Midir.
entities.use: Equip to pledge oneself to the Spears of the Church covenant to be summoned to another players world as a boss.

entities.name: Sunlight Medal
entities.usage: Used to rank up in the Warrior of Sunlight covenant.
entities.desc:
A medal received by members of the Warrior of Sunlight covenant for victory over the final fore when summoned. The summoner also gains the same medal.
The medal, engraved with the holy symbol of the sun, is slightly warm, and reminds one of the great honor of a shared victory.
entities.avail:
• Reward for successfully defeating a boss while in the presence of at least one phantom who is a member of the Warrior of Sunlight covenant.
  • Reward for destroying a Host of Embers as an invader via the use of the Red Eye Orb, where at least one invader present is a member of the Warrior of Sunlight covenant.
  • Lothric Castle
    • One can be found before the fog door that leads to the Dragonslayer Armour, on a corpse next to the elevator that leads back down to the first room after Dancer of the Boreal Valley.
    • Dropped by Lothric Knights.
entities.use: Offer to the Altar of Sunlight in Lothric Castle to rank up in the Warrior of Sunlight covenant.

entities.name: Twinkling Dragon Head Stone
entities.usage: Gain the head of a dragon and emit breath alongside an archdragon mirage.
entities.desc:
Stone imbued with the power of the everlasting dragons, the second of its kind, offered to a towering dragon.
Gain the head of a dragon and emit breath alongside an archdragon mirage. The transformation is irreversible until death.
The illusion achieved was the first case of a human imitating the form of an ancient dragon, and it revealed the smallness of human existence.
The road to the old dragons is long and arduous, and only one can complete the journey.
entities.avail: Obtained by defeating Hawkwood in a duel to the death in the Farron mausoleum at the end of his questline.
entities.use:
Gain the head of a dragon and emit breath alongside an archdragon mirage. However, the transformation is irreversible until death.

The absorption values for the head piece are as follows:

  • 4% Magic
  • 9% Fire
  • -4% Lightning
  • 4% Dark
  • +15 to all status effect resistance

Physical absorption remains at 0%, and all flat defenses remain penalized for the empty armor slot.

entities.name: Twinkling Dragon Torso Stone
entities.usage: Gain the torso of a dragon and roar alongside an archdragon mirage.
entities.desc:
Stone imbued with the power of the everlasting dragons, offered to a towering dragon. This stone shows signs of a nascent light.
Gain the torso of a dragon and roar alongside an archdragon mirage. The transformation is irreversible until death.
Yet true imitation will require a dragon head, as well.
entities.avail: Found at the altar erected at the top of the highest cliff in Archdragon Peak. Pray at the dead archdragon by performing the "Path of the Dragon" gesture in front of the altar to receive the item.
entities.use:
Gain the body of a dragon and roar alongside an archdragon mirage. The transformation is irreversible until death.

Additionally, the player's absorption values for the chest, arms and legs pieces become as follows:

  • 13% Magic
  • 26% Fire
  • -11% Lightning
  • 13% Dark
  • +45 to all status effect resistance

These are compounded with the absorption values of the associated head piece, which is also equipped by default. Physical absorption remains at 0%, and all flat defenses remain penalized for empty armor slots.

entities.name: Undead Bone Shard
entities.usage: Increases the amount of HP recovered from drinking from the Estus Flask.
entities.desc:
Undead bones that yet burn.
Cast it into the shrine bonfire to boost the recovery provided by the Estus Flask.
The bonfire's cinders are bones of Undead, and a bone that still burns is a fresh cinder indeed. Before feeding upon death, one must first pray to it.
entities.avail:
A total of ten Undead Bone Shards can be collected in a single game cycle.

Shard No.Directions
Undead Settlement
1From the Dilapidated Bridge, head toward the cemetery. The shard can be collected from a corpse lying on a segment of floor separated from the cliff and to the right. It is advisable to befriend the giant archer before attempting to get it, though, as the blasts produced by his arrows could send the player into the chasm.
Cathedral of the Deep
2Found on top of a gravestone protruding outside the cliff, in the small graveyard located in front of the cathedral. The area is inhabited by several Infested Corpses. If the player befriended the giant archer in the Undead Settlement, he will lend a hand in clearing this area by shooting arrows.
Farron Keep
3Inside a small structure found to the right of both the main gate and the Keep Ruins bonfire. The building is infested by a large group of Rotten Slugs, so clearing the area with ranged attacks is recommended before even attempting to pick up the shard.
Catacombs of Carthus
4Found within the first Skeleton Boulder that rolls up and down the big staircase. In order to obtain the shard, the player must first kill the hooded skeleton controlling it; the boulder will keep rolling one last time and release the shard upon crashing onto a wall and breaking apart.
Smouldering Lake
5Automatically obtained upon defeating the Carthus Sand Worm.
6Found in the long hallway inhabited by two Demon Clerics after coming from the Demon Ruins bonfire. The shard can be obtained from a corpse lying at the far end corner of this hallway. Special care must be taken before looting the corpse, though, as a Writhing Rotten Flesh will attempt to fall from the ceiling and onto the player if not dealt with first.
Irithyll of the Boreal Valley
7Found outside the Church of Yorshka, behind a large tombstone guarded by a red-eyed Corvian. If the player aided Sirris in defeating Creighton at the beginning of the level, he will invade as a dark spirit in this area.
Profaned Capital
8Found on Laddersmith Gilligan's corpse (along with the Stretch Out gesture) next to the first bonfire.
Lothric Castle
9From the Dragon Barracks, head toward the bridge with the two Wyverns and drop just before reaching the other side to land on a ledge with a corpse holding the shard.
Grand Archives
10The shard can be looted from a corpse sitting on a chair on a ledge above the area with four Scholars on the sixth floor of the library. This ledge can only be reached by entering through a broken window accessible after coming from the roofs section.
entities.use: Cast into the Firelink Shrine bonfire to boost the recovery provided by the Estus Flask.

entities.name: Warrior of Sunlight
entities.usage: Equip to join the Warrior of Sunlight covenant.
entities.desc:
An ancient talisman depicting a holy symbol bestowed upon the Warriors of Sunlight. Equip to pledge oneself to the Warrior of Sunlight covenant.
Warriors of Sunlight are brilliantly beaming co-operators who place their golden signatures to help those in need, for it is their duty to deliver a great conquest to their summoner.
entities.avail:
Found in the Undead Settlement.

From the Undead Settlement bonfire, proceed through the level until reaching a big open area with several praying peasants and an Evangelist. Head to the house on the far left and turn right upon entering. Drop through a hole on the floor partially concealed behind some crates to reach a small kitchen with the talisman and a pot with estus soup.
entities.use: Equip to pledge oneself to the Warrior of Sunlight covenant.

entities.name: Watchdogs of Farron
entities.usage: Equip to join the Watchdogs of Farron covenant.
entities.desc:
Ancient medallion depicting the crest of a wolf. Symbolizes the pact with the Old Wolf of Farron. Equip to pledge oneself to the Watchdogs of Farron.
The Watchdogs ensure that the warriors sleep in serenity, by taking the form of loyal spirits and hunting down those who would trespass the woods of Farron.
Summoning takes place automatically while this is equipped.
entities.avail: Found in the Farron Keep. Obtained by interacting with the Old Wolf of Farron altar in the ruined fortress and accepting to join the Watchdogs of Farron covenant.
entities.use: Equip to pledge oneself to the Watchdogs of Farron covenant. Summoning takes place automatically while this item is equipped.

entities.name: Way of Blue
entities.usage: Equip to join the Way of Blue covenant.
entities.desc:
Pale blue sheepskin parchment featuring an illustration of the moon, symbol of an ancient accord.
Members of the Way of Blue are the beneficiaries of an ancient accord. When a dark spirit threatens them, a blue spirit will grant them assistance, and help to root out the invader.
Summoning takes place automatically while this is equipped.
entities.avail:
• High Wall of Lothric
    • Gifted by Emma, High Priestess of Lothric Castle in the cathedral opposite to Vordt of the Boreal Valley's boss arena, when talking to her after obtaining the Small Lothric Banner.
    • Dropped by Emma if she is killed by the player.
entities.use: Equip to pledge oneself to the Way of Blue covenant. Summoning takes place automatically while this item is equipped.

entities.name: Black Separation Crystal
entities.usage: Returns the player or summoned players to their world.
entities.desc:
A charm of farewell granted to banished Undead. The crystal sends phantoms back to their homes, or you back to yours.
Beware the fickle use of this item if you intend to nurture relations.
entities.avail: Default equipment for all classes.
entities.use:
• When used as a Host of Embers, the player can send any allied phantom back to their own world.
  • When used as a phantom of any type, the player will return to their own world.

entities.name: Cracked Red Eye Orb
entities.page: Cracked Red Eye Orb (Dark Souls III)
entities.usage: Used to invade other worlds at will.
entities.desc:
Online play item.
Invade other worlds at will.
Defeat the Host of Embers of the world you have invaded to gain the strength of the fire.
The Cracked Red Eye Orb is far from perfect, it seems, as Ringfinger Leonhard knows all too well.
entities.avail:
• Can be chosen as a burial gift at the beginning of the game.
  • Firelink Shrine
    • Five are given for free by Ringfinger Leonhard.
    • These are also dropped by Leonhard if he is killed at Firelink Shrine.
  • Farron Keep
    • One and up to three guaranteed drop from Darkwraiths.
entities.use: Use to invade other players. Functions exactly the same as a full Red Eye Orb, but is consumed upon successfully entering another player's world.

entities.name: Divine Spear Fragment
entities.usage: Summons a row of upward-thrusting ritual spears.
entities.desc:
Online play item.
A fragment of the matching ritual spears once held by the knights of Princess Filianore.
These Divine Spears of gold were placed in the trusted hands of exalted Spears.
When Spears of the Church face unduly treacherous foes, this allows them to draw upon former majesty, and summon a row of upward-thrusting ritual spears.
entities.avail:
Obtained as a reward for reaching Rank 2 in the Spears of the Church covenant.

To achieve this, the player must offer 30 Filianore's Spear Ornament to the Divine Spear Monument in the Ringed City.
entities.use: Functions similarly to the Ritual Spear Fragment, but deals twice as much damage. Shares the same active duration and cooldown time.

entities.name: Dried Finger
entities.usage: Allows to summon a third phantom, but also a second dark spirit.
entities.desc:
Online play item.
Dried finger with multiple knuckles.
Use to strength connection to other worlds, allowing the summoning of a third phantom, but also a second dark spirit.
Also makes the summon of a dark spirit occur earlier. Use with caution.
entities.avail: Sold by the Shrine Handmaid in Firelink Shrine for 2,000 souls.
entities.use:
Increases the number of maximum guest players in a Host of Embers' world from 3 to 5. Host will go from a maximum of two summons and one invader for a total of four players, to three summons and two invaders for a total of six players. In territory defender areas (Crucifixion Woods, Irithyll of the Boreal Valley after Pontiff Sulyvahn), the numbers are increased from one phantom and two invaders, to two phantoms and three invaders.

Using the Dried Finger will also move the host's world to the top of the invasion priority queue and reset the cooldown timer for being invaded, while also decreasing the minimum interval for subsequent invasions. As well, whenever a host-allied phantom enters the world (whether by being summoned via White Sign Soapstone or by covenant through Way of Blue), the invasion cooldown timer is immediately reset.

entities.name: Red Eye Orb
entities.usage: Invade other worlds at will.
entities.desc:
Online play item.
Invade other worlds at will.
Defeat the Host of Embers of the world you have invaded to gain the strength of the fire.
The Red Eye Orb is rooted in a tiny land swallowed by darkness long ago. Some choose to put the orb to other uses. To embark on this path, enter the service of Rosaria in the Cathedral of the Deep.
entities.avail:
The player must defeat a Darkwraith located at the bottom of a tower in the High Wall of Lothric after receiving the Lift Chamber Key provided by Ringfinger Leonhard once they have obtained a Pale Tongue.

From the Tower on the Wall bonfire, make way to the bottom of the tower and unlock the barred door with the key given by Leonhard. Ride the lift down and fight the Darkwraith there. The item will be automatically added to the player's inventory once he dies.
entities.use:
Using this infinite consumable will allow a player to invade another player's world as a dark spirit. A Host of Embers can only be invaded in this manner if the boss for the area is still alive. Unlike in the first Dark Souls, usage of this item is not restricted to any specific covenant, and victory requirements will vary depending on the covenant that the player has pledged themselves to.

Invasion ranges can also vary depending on covenant status. In all cases, invasion range is based on the player's Soul Level.

Invasion typeLower LimitUpper Limit
Red Spirit (below level 351)90% of player's Soul Level110% of player's Soul Level + 20
Mound-makers (below level 351)90% of player's Soul Level115% of player's Soul Level + 20
Any (level 351 and higher)Soul Level 351None

entities.name: Red Sign Soapstone
entities.usage: Create a hostile red invasion sign.
entities.desc:
Online play item.
Create a hostile red invasion sign.
Be summoned to another world as a dark spirit, and defeat the Host of Embers to gain the strength of fire.
Not all dark spirits are unsporting, or they wouldn't make use of this soapstone.
entities.avail: Obtained after killing the non-hostile Man-grub outside of Rosaria's Bed Chamber in the Cathedral of the Deep.
entities.use: Creates a red summon sign, allowing others to invite the player into their world as a dark spirit.

entities.name: Ritual Spear Fragment
entities.usage: Summons a row of upward-thrusting ritual spears.
entities.desc:
Online play item.
A fragment of the matching ritual spears once held by the knights of Princess Filianore.
They are the namesake of the Spears of the Church.
When Spears of the Church face unduly treacherous foes, this allows them to draw upon former majesty, and summon a row of upward-thrusting ritual spears.
entities.avail: Found on a corpse outside of the Church of Filianore, near the greatswords-wielding Ringed Knight.
entities.use:
Upon use, the wielder brandishes their weapon forward, gaining the Perseverance effect immediately upon item use. After a short delay, during which the ground in front of the wielder glows, a row of upwardly-thrusting spears encased in lightning are conjured, surging forward. The spears persist for several seconds, acting as a barrier that damages foes that walk into them, though allowing free movement to the wielder.

This item does not require Focus Points to cast, but has a cooldown inbetween uses. The cooldown reduces in tandem with the number of summoned phantoms present.

entities.name: Roster of Knights
entities.usage: Allows to check the Blade of the Darkmoon leaderboard.
entities.desc:
Online play item. A roster of knights of the Darkmoon who have served since the age of the old Royals.
Use to discover the names of Darkmoon Knights, an order of elite knights shrouded in shadows.
entities.avail: Found in Irithyll of the Boreal Valley. From the Church of Yorshka, head towards the graveyard and turn right before exiting the church. The roster can be found on a corpse next to the staircase.
entities.use: The Roster of Knights allows the player to check the Blade of the Darkmoon leaderboard.

entities.name: Way of White Circlet
entities.usage: Restores connection to other worlds.
entities.desc:
Online play item.
Restore the connection to other worlds.
Those who engage in unjust deeds when in contact with other worlds will lose their connection to them.
Way of White Circlets assume such sin as their own, but are found few and far between. Acting without honor will never be without risk.
entities.avail: A single circlet is included within the player's inventory at the beginning of the game. A new Way of White Circlet can be found in the beginning grave in Cemetery of Ash after an unknown number of gameplay hours, once the previous one has been consumed.
entities.use: If a player disconnects from a PvP session too many times, their online matchmaking will be disabled. Using the Way of White Circlet restores the player's connection to other worlds.

entities.name: White Sign Soapstone
entities.usage: Creates a co-op summon sign.
entities.desc:
Online play item.
Create a co-op summon sign.
Be summoned to another world as a phantom through your sign, and defeat the area boss to gain the strength of flame.
The nature of Lothric is murky, unclear.
The White Sign Soapstone allows Unkindled to assist one another.
entities.avail: Sold by the Shrine Handmaid in Firelink Shrine for 500 souls.
entities.use: Lays a white summon sign on the ground. A Host of Embers may interact with this sign to summon the sign's owner into their world.

entities.name: Fading Soul
entities.usage: Consume to acquire 50 souls.
entities.desc:
The fading soul of a corpse.
Use to gain a smattering of souls.
Let the Fire Keeper transform this sovereignless soul into a source of strength, for to be Unkindled is to be a vessel for souls.
entities.avail:
A minimum of seven are guaranteed to be found per playthrough.

  • Cemetery of Ash
    • Dropped by Gravetender Hollows.
  • Undead Settlement
    • On the path to the Hollow Manservant that transports the player to the Pit of Hollows, there is a rooftop zone patrolled by numerous Thralls. A corpse in the open holds the item, as a trap for the Thralls to ambush the player.
    • In the cemetery beyond the Dilapidated Bridge bonfire, on a corpse at the base of the White Birch tree guarded by the Giant Archer of the Undead Settlement.
    • Dropped by Cage Spiders. (×5)
  • Road of Sacrifices
    • On the wooded path leading to the Crucifixion Woods bonfire. It is held by a corpse near a stone archway that serves as an ambush for a Starved Hound.
  • Cathedral of the Deep
    • At the extreme end of the graveyard, on a corpse near the Executioner's Greatsword.
  • Irithyll of the Boreal Valley
    • Outside the Church of Yorshka. The item is found on a corpse dangling from the edge of a cliff, to lure players into an ambush by Irithyllian Slaves.
    • A second one is found further up the path to the right, at the base of a tree before the lone red-eyed Corvian.
  • Irithyll Dungeon
    • Shortly after encountering the first Jailer, there is a corpse holding the item dangling from a ledge to the left. It is a trap laid for a Reanimated Corpse to ambush the player from an open cell on the right and knock the player down to the lower floor.
    • Dropped by Cage Spiders. (×5)
  • Untended Graves
    • Dropped by Gravetender Hollows.

entities.avail:
Fifteen can be found in each playthrough.

  • Farron Keep
    • In the farthest reaches of the swamp, close to the flame patrolled by Elder Ghrus. In the deep waters populated by Basilisks, a corpse can be spotted due to its outstretched hand sticking out of the water. The soul item can be looted from it.
    • In the same area as above, close to where Yellowfinger Heysel invades the player, there is an alcove near the stairs that lead up to the flame from the deep swamp. Another drowned corpse here holds the item.
  • Catacombs of Carthus
    • Amidst the field of bones before the suspension bridge that leads to High Lord Wolnir are two corpses. One of the corpses holds the item.
    • In the path beneath the suspension bridge leading to Smouldering Lake guarded by the Fire Demon and several resurrecting skeletons, one of the corpses on the lowest tier can be looted for the consumable.
  • Irithyll of the Boreal Valley
    • Found on a corpse close to the Central Irithyll bonfire, next to a nearby outer railing.
    • In the courtyard after the initial wave of Pontiff Knights is a fountain patrolled by Irithyllian Slaves and which a Fire Witch will approach towards. Next to the fountain are two corpses, one of which holds the item.
    • Once the main road diverges and a small side path to the left grants access to the Church of Yorshka, there is a corpse propped up against a statue on the left side right before the central plaza with the Fire Witch and Pontiff Knights, which can be looted for the consumable.
    • On a corpse within the dried riverbed past the Church of Yorshka. The corpse resides on one of the islands along the path to the Distant Manor.
    • Beyond the Distant Manor, in an alleyway leading back up to the main Irithyll plaza, there is a tree near which the Londor Pale Shade will invade the player if they are not in good graces with Yuria of Londor. At the base of the tree is a corpse holding the item.
  • Irithyll Dungeon
    • Within the initial cell block, in the wing that contains the Jailbreaker's Key shortcut there is a lone corpse on the lower floor that is guarded by an Infested Corpse. The corpse can be looted for the item.
    • Upon reaching the bottom-most cell block patrolled by multiple Jailers and leading to the Profaned Capital, an elevator can be accessed which grants access to a shortcut back to the initial cell block. Close to the door which can be unlocked to facilitate the shortcut is a corpse holding the consumable.
  • Lothric Castle
    • Upon dropping down into the moat in the Dragon Barracks that is below the perch of the two Lothric Wyverns, a path to the right leads around and back to the bonfire. After dealing with the Hollow Assassins that guard this path, a corpse dangling from the ledge that drops down to the bonfire can be looted for the item.
    • Found on a corpse in the area to the left of the moat path. Prior to crossing the open keep to the powder barrel room, the corpse can be found leaning against a column in the open, near the stairs that lead down to the Boreal Outrider Knight.
    • In the powder barrel room, there is a ladder that leads to the foot of one of the Lothric Wyverns. At the top of the ladder is a corpse dangling over the ledge which can be looted for the soul.
  • Archdragon Peak
    • In the Ancient Wyvern battle arena, on a corpse in the open path beneath the Wyvern's landing zone. It can be found in the area leading towards the building where the first wave of Man Serpents are encountered.

entities.avail:
A maximum of nine are guaranteed to be obtained by the player in each playthrough.

  • One is granted to the player at the start of the game by choosing the "Sovereignless Soul" burial gift.
  • Undead Settlement
    • At the top of the tower inhabited by the Giant Archer of the Undead Settlement, there is a corpse holding the item in a small alcove opposite to the lever that controls the elevator.
  • Farron Keep
    • Near the white tree patrolled by a Great Crab and which is guarded by the Giant Archer of the Undead Settlement, a drowned corpse can be looted for the item.
  • Cathedral of the Deep
    • On the rooftops portion of the exterior of the cathedral, there is a small side structure after navigating the flying buttresses that is patrolled by a large number of Thralls. Inside of the structure is a corpse holding the soul, though additional Thralls lie in ambush.
    • In the interior of the cathedral, there is a path after the first shortcut back to the Cleansing Chapel that is guarded by a large Giant Slave. One of the corpses along this route holds the item.
    • On the bottom floor of the cathedral interior, within the sludge at the feet of the first Giant Slave. A corpse beneath the Giant Slave and near to the large double doors holds the consumable.
  • Catacombs of Carthus
    • At the bottom of the ladder in the first section of the tomb, a corpse sitting against a wall holds the item.
    • A lone pathway to the right after some stairs past the initial bridge is guarded by two headless skeletons. Beyond these two skeletons is a corpse holding the soul consumable.
  • Grand Archives
    • Held by a corpse within the dark room after the first wax pool, against some bookshelves against the back wall and protected by Clawed Curses.
  • Archdragon Peak
    • Past the initial gauntlet and ascending the stairs after the first bonfire, a corpse dangling off of a ledge to the right can be looted for the item.
  • The Ringed City
    • Dropped by White-faced Locusts.

bosses.intro: The short version of each boss page's strategy, answer first. The wiki's full text is behind Full strategy.

bosses.t: Hit him while he rises after you pull the Coiled Sword: he cannot retaliate until he takes up his weapon. Keep a medium distance, roll behind him or through his slow, poorly tracking attacks, and punish with several hits. Most of his attacks make him pause to recover.

Get directly behind him and attack in short bursts: his turns leave gaps to punish. Dodge rather than block, since blocking costs a lot of stamina. At about half health he charges three times in a row; dodge them, then run behind him while he breathes frost and punish.

Attack the growths on its body: only they take damage, and the belly growth is the easiest. Dodge its well-telegraphed attacks and ignore the hollows. In the second phase a white hand grabs from the front, so stay at its side.

Run up and hit rapidly: this interrupts its spells and makes it teleport. Do not block the spells (large stamina drain). From half health it spawns clones that die to a single hit, so pack throwing knives; the real Sage casts purple spells, the clones blue.

Only killing the Deacon with the red aura damages the boss health bar, so path around the crowd and go straight for the glowing one. When Archdeacon Royce appears, kill the two blue-robed Deacons first: they are stronger, heal Royce and do not respawn.

Fight defensively while the red-eyed Watchers that awaken attack the others; they deal damage and draw the main Watcher's attacks away from you. The main Watcher is fast and jumps around, so never let your guard down. Phase two adds fire trails that erupt into pillars of flame; dying there resets the whole fight.

Destroy his three bracelets (one on the right hand, two on the left) and he descends into the Abyss and dies. Stay out of the black fog around him and get out of range when he exhales it. Bows work well for the right-hand bracelet, which is more often in the fog.

Move behind the boss to evade both its hammer swings and its cone of fire. Sprint away from the flame wave instead of rolling through the ring. Hide behind the demon corpse piles from the meteor shower. Below 20% it collapses and charges a large explosion: stay back until it goes off.

Roll behind him: only his turning pirouette attacks (and plunge attacks in phase two) hit behind his back. Do not swing more than twice before you dodge. He is extremely susceptible to parrying, each riposte dealing upwards of 1000 damage. From half health a phantom copy performs each move moments before he does.

Pick up the Storm Ruler beside his throne and use its skill, Storm King: hold the stance for a few seconds, then slam it for huge ranged damage. Most other weapons barely hurt him. If you finished Siegward's questline, Siegward joins the fight with his own Storm Ruler.

Charge him at the start to avoid his soul spear, get behind him and focus his tail. At about 55%-60% health he comes back buffed with fire and his arrows follow you; Twisted Wall of Light can negate his ranged attacks. Blue Bug and Red Bug Pellets are recommended.

Stay near her right leg so the grab is easy to see, and use stamina reinforcers such as the Chloranthy Ring. Around half health she draws a second blade and her combos get longer with unpredictable stops; stay in front of her there and use fast weapons without long windup.
Roll away from its attacks and land one of your own; blocking costs a huge amount of stamina. Stay under 70% Equip Load for a fast roll. Do not get greedy with attacks.

Phase one: rush to his hind legs and attack, since most attacks land in front of him. After about 40% of his health, keep distance and let him attack first; after his lunge he roars and is completely vulnerable, so rush after him and hit his face until he staggers for a critical attack.

Score hits at the start: he is vulnerable from the first moment. Watch for combos with a delayed finishing attack meant to make you roll early. In phase two, run away when a combo starts and hit him once or twice as he recovers from a jumping attack. Heal behind him just after a combo ends.

Skip the fight: sprint under the wyvern and left through the ruins, cross the stone bridge and the wooden platforms, then drop to the platform above it and perform a plunging attack that instantly slays it. Missing the hit means falling to your death.

Phase one: aim every attack at the mount's head or at the rider. Phase two: his attacks are dragged out to catch you rolling too early, so wait for him to finish a combo and attack during his recovery.

bosses.boss: Lorian, Elder Prince and Lothric, Younger Prince
bosses.t: Phase one: stay near Lorian, get in one or two quick swings during his short recoveries and roll; fast weapons such as straight swords work best, and he is extremely weak to Lightning (Gold Pine Resin, Lightning Blade). Phase two: get behind Lorian during his attacks and strike Lothric directly.

s.title: Lorian, Elder Prince and Lothric, Younger Prince

bosses.t: Finish phase one quickly to save Estus: pressure the boss and attack constantly until it staggers. In phase two, keep distance and bait out the jump attack, which is easily avoidable and leaves it open for a hit or two; up close you risk the grab and the five-hit combo.

Kill the three wolves with the Gravetender first. Use a big weapon such as an ultra greatsword to stagger him and break his guard. Once the Greatwolf joins, finish the Gravetender as quickly as possible, and do not block the wolf's charges with anything less than a greatshield.

Phase one: learn her patterns behind a high-stability greatshield and never go for more than one or two hits; she nearly always jumps away after that. When she turns invisible, run straight at her to make her reappear. Phase two: Father Ariandel and Friede share one health bar.

He is fought in the second phase of the Sister Friede fight (see that page). He is very aggressive but not particularly fast; avoid his bowl and the charge that crushes you with his legs. He can be staggered and riposted after enough damage to his arms.

Phase one: split the two demons up and keep both in view. An Extinguished demon is slow and easy to slay; if both are Ignited, play passively and kite them until one performs the fiery slam and reverts. Enough poise damage staggers a demon for a visceral attack.

Kill the two Church Guardians Argo summons when you can: they heal the Spear with Great Heal, and they can be parried and riposted. Vow of Silence blocks their healing miracle. Ignore Judicator Argo; killing him has no benefits.
Target his head: the rest of his body has strong defenses, and hitting legs and tail takes about twice as many hits. Stay strictly centered with Midir so his size does not throw off the camera.

Count the hits it takes to stagger him (usually three with great weapons): a stagger stuns him out of his hard-hitting combos. In the second and third phase a stagger from hitting him directly on the head lets you riposte him. When he rears back with a groan, expect several powerful strikes ending in a high leap plunge. Dodge toward him so his cape does not hit you after the roll.

builds.intro: Built from wiki data: soft caps from two wikis, the infusion from the Infusion page, rings chosen by their effect text, and every weapon whose base scaling fits. Which rings make the list and the stat targets are the guide's own choice, read off those pages. The Creators box names an item only when two or more creators named it recently.

caps.t: Vigor levels 11 to 27 give 23 to 44 HP each; levels 28 to 49 give 5 to 19 HP; levels 50 to 99 give only 1 to 3 HP. The biggest gain in the wiki table, 44 HP per level, is at 16 and 17 Vigor.
FP per point is highest up to 35 Attunement, then drops. Slots come at 10, 14, 18 and more.
Stamina grows until 40 Endurance; past 40 you need 5 or more levels for each extra point.
Each level adds 1.0 to maximum equip load all the way to 99. Raise it only until your armor and weapons fit.
Damage per point drops after 40 and again after 60. Two-handing multiplies Strength by 1.5, so 27 reaches the 40 cap.

Both wikis put the first Dexterity soft cap at 40. The second Dexterity soft cap differs between them, 80 on the Dark Souls Wiki (as of the 1.32 regulation) and 60 on Fextralife. Casting speed stops improving at 50.

caps.cap: 40 (Fextralife) / minor cap 45, gains until 60 (Dark Souls Wiki); 30 for Dark or Chaos infusions
caps.t: Weapons with innate Magic damage and Crystal or Simple infusions soft-cap at 40 Intelligence. Weapons infused with a Chaos Gem or Dark Gem soft-cap at 30 Intelligence, along with 30 Faith. For staves the two wikis differ: Fextralife gives spell damage a soft cap at 40 and a sharper cap at 60; the Dark Souls Wiki says staves keep gaining until 60 Intelligence, with a minor soft cap at 45. Dark catalysts such as the Izalith Staff and Sunless Talisman improve up to 45 Intelligence and 45 Faith.

caps.cap: 40 for weapons; catalysts 40, 45 or 60 (Fextralife) / gains until 60, slower past 45 (Dark Souls Wiki); 30 for Dark or Chaos infusions
caps.t: Lightning weapons and weapons infused with a Lightning Gem or Blessed Gem soft-cap at 40 Faith. Infusions with a Chaos Gem or Dark Gem soft-cap at 30 Faith alongside 30 Intelligence. For miracle catalysts the two wikis differ: Fextralife gives a miracle soft cap of 40, 45 or 60 depending on the catalyst; the Dark Souls Wiki says talismans and chimes improve up until 60 Faith, and most fall off after 45 Faith. Dark catalysts use 45 Faith and 45 Intelligence.

caps.cap: 50 for bleed build-up (Fextralife); no damage soft cap given
caps.t: Luck raises item discovery and bleed build-up on regular and Blood-infused weapons. Fextralife says bleed build-up has its best gains between 25 and 50 Luck, where 50 is the hard cap. Hollow-infused weapons scale with Luck; neither wiki gives a soft cap for that damage.

idea.t: Big weapons, heavy hits that break an enemy's poise and stagger it. Two-hand to get the 1.5 Strength bonus.

stats.t: Vigor 27 first, Endurance toward 40, Strength 40, then Vigor toward 50.
